35: def unbalanced(text: str) -> Optional[str]:
36:     """Why ``text`` has unbalanced brackets, or None when it is balanced.
37: 
38:     Mathematica strings ("...") and comments ((* ... *), nested) are skipped. An
39:     unbalanced verbatim string renders into a .fr that FeynRules stops reading
40:     with "Unexpected end of file" or "Invalid syntax", long after the schema
41:     said OK.

43:     stack: List[Tuple[str, int]] = []
44:     i, n, depth = 0, len(text), 0
45:     while i < n:
46:         c = text[i]
47:         if depth:                                  # inside a comment
48:             if text.startswith("(*", i):
49:                 depth, i = depth + 1, i + 2
50:             elif text.startswith("*)", i):
51:                 depth, i = depth - 1, i + 2
52:             else:
53:                 i += 1
54:             continue
55:         if text.startswith("(*", i):
56:             depth, i = 1, i + 2
57:             continue

59:             i += 1

61:                 i += 2 if text[i] == "\\" else 1
62:             if i >= n:

64:             i += 1
65:             continue

404: def topo_sort_parameters(params: List[Parameter]) -> List[Parameter]:

408:     dependency cycle.

63: \begin{abstract}
64: Motivated by TeV-scale neutrino mass models, we propose a systematic treatment of heavy neutrino $(N)$ production at hadron colliders.
65: 
66: Our simple and efficient modeling of the vector boson fusion (VBF) $W^\pm\gamma\rightarrow N\ell^\pm$ and $N\ell^\pm+nj$ signal definitions
67: resolve collinear and soft divergences that have plagued past studies, and is applicable to other color-singlet processes, 
68: e.g., associated Higgs $(W^\pm h)$,  sparticle $(\tilde{\ell}^\pm\tilde{\nu_\ell})$, and charged Higgs $(h^{\pm\pm}h^{\mp})$ production.
69: 
70: We present, for the first time, a comparison of all leading $N$ production modes, 
71: including both gluon fusion (GF) $gg\rightarrow Z^*/h^*\rightarrow N\overset{(-)}{\nu_\ell}$ and VBF.
72: 
73: We obtain fully differential results up to next-to-leading order (NLO) in QCD accuracy 
74: using a Monte Carlo tool chain linking FeynRules, N{\small LO}CT, and MadGraph5\_aMC@NLO.
75: Associated model files are publicly available.
76: At the 14 TeV LHC, the leading order GF rate is small and comparable to the NLO $N\ell^\pm+1j$ rate;
77: at a future 100 TeV Very Large Hadron Collider, GF dominates for $m_N={300-1500}$ GeV, beyond which VBF takes lead.
78: \end{abstract}

87: \section{Introduction}\label{sec:Intro}
88: 
89: The origin of neutrino masses $m_\nu$ that are tiny compared to all other fermion masses is a broad issue
90: in particle physics, cosmology, and astrophysics.
91: Nonzero $m_\nu$ imply the existence of new particles~\cite{Ma:1998dn},
92: but more generally, physics beyond the Standard Model (BSM) that may be observable at current and future experiments.
93: Extended neutrino mass 
94: models~\cite{Pilaftsis:1991ug,Kersten:2007vk,Gu:2008yj,Dev:2009aw,Zhang:2009ac,Adhikari:2010yt,Chen:2013fna,Dev:2013oxa,Dev:2015vra} based on the
95: Type I~\cite{Minkowski:1977sc,Yanagida:1979as,VanNieuwenhuizen:1979hm,Ramond:1979py,Glashow:1979nm,Mohapatra:1979ia,
96: GellMann:1980vs,Schechter:1980gr,Shrock:1980ct,Schechter:1981cv}, 
97: Inverse~\cite{Mohapatra:1986aw,Mohapatra:1986bd,Bernabeu:1987gr}, and 
98: Linear Seesaw Mechanisms~\cite{Akhmedov:1995ip,Akhmedov:1995vm}, 
99: feature heavy mass eigenstates $N_{i}$ that couple to electroweak (EW) bosons via mixing with left-handed (LH) neutrinos $\nu_{L}$.
100: In these TeV-scale scenarios, active-sterile mixing can be as large as  $\vert V_{\ell N_i}\vert\sim10^{-3}-10^{-2}$, 
101: and consistent with oscillation and EW data~\cite{Atre:2009rg,Antusch:2014woa,deGouvea:2015euy},
102: as well as direct searches by the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) experiments~\cite{Aaij:2014aba,Aad:2015xaa,Khachatryan:2016olu}.
103: Thus, if kinematically accessible, 
104: hadron colliders can produce heavy neutrinos that
105: decay to lepton number- and/or flavor-violating final states with observable rates.
106: 
107: 
108: 
109: For heavy $N$ masses $m_N$ above the EW scale, a systematic comparison of all leading single $N$ production modes cataloged 
110: in~\cite{Keung:1983uu,Datta:1993nm} has never been performed.
111: Most investigations focus on the charge current (CC) Drell-Yan (DY) 
112: process~\cite{Keung:1983uu,Pilaftsis:1991ug,Han:2006ip,delAguila:2006bda,delAguila:2007qnc,Atre:2009rg},
113: as shown in Fig.~\ref{fig:diagrams}(a),
114: \begin{equation}
115:  q ~\overline{q'} \rightarrow W^* \rightarrow N ~\ell^\pm, ~\quad q \in \{u,c,d,s,b\},
116:  \label{eq:DYCC}
117: \end{equation}
118: and has recently been found to be subleading in parts of this mass regime~\cite{Hessler:2014ssa,Alva:2014gxa}.
119: Missing in most analyses is the gluon fusion (GF) channel~\cite{Hessler:2014ssa},
120: which proceeds at leading order (LO) through quark triangles in Fig.~\ref{fig:diagrams}(b),
121: \begin{equation}
122:  g ~g \rightarrow h^*/Z^* \rightarrow N ~ \overset{(-)}{\nu_\ell}.
123:  \label{eq:GF}
124: \end{equation}
125: Variants of Eq.~(\ref{eq:GF}) have been studied elsewhere~\cite{BhupalDev:2012zg,Batell:2015aha}.
126: Formally, GF is a finite next-to-next-to-leading order in QCD correction to the neutral current (NC) DY process
127: \begin{eqnarray}
128:  q ~\overline{q} \rightarrow Z^* \rightarrow N ~\overset{(-)}{\nu_\ell}.
129:  \label{eq:DYNC}
130: \end{eqnarray}
131: 
132: Recent analyses have investigated the sizable EW vector boson fusion (VBF) 
133: process~\cite{Dev:2013wba,Bambhaniya:2014hla,Alva:2014gxa,Deppisch:2015qwa,Ng:2015hba,Arganda:2015ija,Das:2015toa}:
134: \begin{equation}
135:  q_{1} ~q_{2} ~\overset{W\gamma+WZ~\text{Fusion}}{\longrightarrow} ~N ~\ell^\pm ~q_{1}' ~q_{2}',
136:  \label{eq:VBF}
137: \end{equation}
138: and subleading CC DY with $n\geq1$ QCD jets~\cite{Dev:2013wba,Das:2014jxa,Das:2015toa}:
139: \begin{equation}
140:  p ~p \rightarrow W^{*}+ nj \rightarrow N\ell^\pm+  nj, \quad p,j\in\{\overset{(-)}{q},g\},
141:  \label{eq:DYnj}
142: \end{equation}
143: but with conflicting results.
144: The last two processes are plagued by soft and collinear poles in $s$- and $t$-channel exchanges of massless gauge bosons, 
145: issues usually associated with perturbative QCD, and require care~\cite{Alva:2014gxa,Ruiz:2015zca}.
146: E.g., inadequately regulated diverges are responsible for the overestimated 
147: cross sections claimed in~\cite{Dev:2013wba,Das:2014jxa,Deppisch:2015qwa,Das:2015toa}
148: 
149: 
150: We introduce a treatment that resolves all these issues.
151: Our results have widespread implications for SM and BSM physics:
152: the prescriptions for Eqs.~(\ref{eq:VBF}) and (\ref{eq:DYnj}) are applicable to, among other processes,
153: associated Higgs $(W^\pm h)$,  sparticle $(\tilde{\ell}^\pm\tilde{\nu_\ell})$, and charged Higgs $(h^{\pm\pm}h^{\mp})$ production.
154: 
155: To date, our study is the most accurate and comprehensive presentation of heavy $N$ production mechanisms at colliders.
156: It represents the first time properties of infrared and collinear (IRC) safety have been so rigorously imposed in this context, particularly to VBF.
157: 
158: Furthermore, we obtain modest next-to-leading order (NLO) in QCD corrections, demonstrating the stability of our approach.
159: 
160: \begin{figure*}[!th]
161: \includegraphics[width=0.90\textwidth]{feynmanDiagrams.eps}
162: \caption{Heavy neutrino production via (a) charge (neutral) current Drell-Yan, (b) gluon fusion, and (c) $W\gamma$ fusion.}
163: \label{fig:diagrams}
164: \end{figure*}
165: 
166: We guarantee the perturbativity of the VBF process by factorizing and resumming the $t$-channel $\gamma$
167: into a DGLAP-evolved parton distribution function (PDF).
168: Using a $\gamma$-PDF, one considers instead, as shown in Fig.~\ref{fig:diagrams}(c),
169: \begin{equation}
170:  q ~\gamma \rightarrow N ~\ell^\pm ~q'.
171: \end{equation}
172: $WZ$ fusion is subleading and can be neglected~\cite{Alva:2014gxa}.
173: 
174: We regularize Eq.~(\ref{eq:DYnj}) by imposing transverse momentum $(p_T)$ cuts consistent with Collins-Soper-Sterman (CSS) 
175: $p_T$-resummation~\cite{Collins:1984kg}.
176: 
177: Our Monte Carlo (MC) framework allows us to compute fully differential Feynman diagrams up to one loop, 
178: and therefore GF at LO and the remaining processes at NLO;
179: only Eq.~(\ref{eq:DYCC}) has been evaluated before at NLO~\cite{Ruiz:2015gsa,Das:2016hof}.
180: 
181: 
182: 
183: At the 14 TeV LHC, the CC DY channel prevails for $N$ masses $m_N=150-850\GeV$; above this, the VBF cross section is larger.
184: However, due to the $gg$ luminosity increase, GF is the leading mechanism at a hypothetical future 100 TeV Very Large Hadron Collider (VLHC)
185: for $m_N = {300-1500}\GeV$; at higher $m_N$, VBF dominates.
186: 
187: 
188: We now introduce our theoretical model, computation procedure,
189: and signal definition prescription.
190: After presenting and discussing results, we conclude.
191: 
192: 
193: 
194: 
195: 
196: 
197: \section{Heavy Neutrino Model}\label{sec:Theory}
198: 
199: For  
200: $i~(m) =1,\dots,3$, LH (light) states and 
201: $j~(m')=1,\dots,n$, right-handed (heavy) states,
202: chiral neutrinos can be expanded into mass eigenstates by the rotation
203: \begin{eqnarray}
204: \begin{pmatrix} \nu_{Li} \\  N_{Rj}^c \end{pmatrix}
205: =
206: \begin{pmatrix} 
207: U_{3\times3} && V_{3\times n} \\
208: X_{n\times3} && Y_{n\times n}
209: \end{pmatrix}
210: \begin{pmatrix} \nu_{m} \\ N_{m'}^c \end{pmatrix}.
211: \end{eqnarray}
212: After rotating the charged leptons into the mass basis, 
213: which we take to be the identity matrix for simplicity,
214: $U_{3 \times3}$ is the observed light neutrino mixing matrix and
215: $V_{3 \times n}$ parameterizes active-heavy mixing. 
216: In the notation of~\cite{Atre:2009rg}, the flavor state $\nu_{\ell}$ in the mass basis is
217: \begin{equation}
218:  \nu_{\ell} = \sum_{m=1}^{3} U_{\ell m}\nu_{m} + \sum_{m'=1}^{n}V_{\ell m'} N^{c}_{m'}.
219: \end{equation}
220: For simplicity, we consider only one heavy mass eigenstate, labeled by $N$. This does not affect our conclusions.
221: The interaction Lagrangian with EW bosons is then
222: \begin{eqnarray}
223:   \mathcal{L}_{\rm Int.} = 
224:   &-& \frac{g}{\sqrt{2}}W^+_\mu		\sum_{\ell=e}^\tau \sum_{m=1}^3 ~\overline{\nu_m} ~U_{\ell m}^*	~\gamma^\mu P_L\ell^-\nonumber\\
225:   &-& \frac{g}{\sqrt{2}}W^+_\mu		\sum_{\ell=e}^\tau 		~\overline{N^c} ~V_{\ell N}^* 	~\gamma^\mu P_L\ell^-\nonumber\\
226:   &-& \frac{g}{2\cos\theta_W}Z_\mu	\sum_{\ell=e}^\tau \sum_{m=1}^3	~\overline{\nu_m} ~U_{\ell m}^*	~\gamma^\mu P_L\nu_\ell\nonumber\\
227:   &-& \frac{g}{2\cos\theta_W}Z_\mu	\sum_{\ell=e}^\tau 		~\overline{N^c} ~V_{\ell N}^*	~\gamma^\mu P_L\nu_\ell\nonumber\\
228:   &-& \frac{g m_N}{2M_W} h	\sum_{\ell=e}^\tau 		~\overline{N^c} ~V_{\ell N}^*	 P_L\nu_\ell + \text{H.c.}
229:   \label{eq:Lagrangian}
230: \end{eqnarray}
231: 
232: 
233: Precise values of $V_{\ell N}$ are model-dependent and are constrained by oscillation and collider experiments, 
234: tests of lepton universality, and $0\nu\beta\beta$-decay~\cite{Atre:2009rg,Antusch:2014woa,deGouvea:2015euy}.
235: However, $V_{\ell N}$ factorize in $N$ production cross sections such that
236: \begin{equation}
237:  \sigma(pp\rightarrow N~X) = \vert V_{N\ell}\vert^2 ~\times~ \sigma_{0}(pp\rightarrow N~X),
238: \end{equation}
239: where $\sigma_{0}$ is a model-independent ``bare'' cross section in which one sets $\vert V_{N\ell}\vert=1$.
240: Hence, our results are applicable to various heavy neutrino models.
241: 
242: 
243: 
244: \section{Computational Setup}\label{sec:MC}
245: 
246: We implement the above Lagrangian with Goldstone boson couplings in the Feynman gauge into FeynRules (FR) 2.3.10~\cite{Alloul:2013bka,Christensen:2008py}.
247: QCD renormalization and $R_2$ rational counterterms are calculated with \nloct~1.02 (prepackaged in FR)~\cite{Degrande:2014vpa} 
248: and FeynArts 3.8~\cite{Hahn:2000kx}.
249: Feynman rules are collected into a universal output file (UFO)~\cite{Degrande:2011ua} and is available publicly~\cite{nloFRModel}.
250: We obtain fully differential results using MadGraph5$\_$aMC$@$NLO  2.3.3~\cite{Alwall:2014hca}.
251: SM inputs are taken from the 2014 Particle Data Group~\cite{Agashe:2014kda}:
252: \begin{eqnarray}
253:  \alpha^{\rm \overline{MS}}(M_{Z})		&=& 1/127.940, \quad M_{Z}=91.1876\GeV, \nonumber\\ 
254:  \sin^{2}_{\rm \overline{MS}}(\theta_{W}) 	&=& 0.23126.
255:  \label{eq:smInputs}
256: \end{eqnarray}
257: We assume five massless quarks, take the Cabbibo-Kobayashi-Masakawa (CKM) matrix to be diagonal with unit entries,
258: and use the NLO NNPDF2.3 QED PDF (\texttt{lhaid:244600}) ~\cite{Ball:2013hta},
259: which features a $\gamma$-PDF with both elastic and inelastic components,
260: at collider energies of $\sqrt{s}=14$ and $100$ TeV. 
261: We extract $\alpha_s(\mu_r^2)$ from the PDFs.
262: 
263: 
264: 
265: 
266: \section{Infrared- and Collinear-Safe Hadron Collider Signal Definitions}\label{sec:SigDef}
267: 
268: To consistently compare channels and colliders, 
269: we follow the 2013 Snowmass recommendations~\cite{Avetisyan:2013onh}
270: and evaluate cross sections assuming the same fiducial acceptance.
271: In practice, however, one tunes cuts to specific colliders and final states.
272: Jet and charged lepton pseudorapidities $(\eta^{j,\ell})$ and charged lepton $p_T$ are required to satisfy~\cite{Avetisyan:2013onh}:
273: \begin{equation}
274:  \vert\eta^{j,\ell}\vert < 2.5, \quad p_T^\ell > 20\GeV.
275:  \label{eq:LepCuts}
276: \end{equation}
277: QCD radiation in Eq.~(\ref{eq:DYnj}) gives rise to fixed order (FO) cross sections that scale as powers of $\log(Q^2/q_T^2)$:
278: \begin{equation}
279:  \sigma(pp\rightarrow N\ell^\pm+nj) \sim \sum^n_k \alpha_s^k(Q^2)\log^{(2k-1)}\left(\frac{Q^2}{q_T^2}\right).
280:  \label{eq:qcdPowerSeries}
281: \end{equation}
282: $Q\sim m_N$ is the scale of the hard scattering process
283: and $q_T \equiv \sum_k^n p_{T,k}^{j}$ is the $(N\ell)$-system's transverse momentum,
284: which equals the sum of all jet $p_T$.
285: 
286: The perturbativity of these logarithms for TeV-scale leptons was studied in~\cite{Ruiz:2015zca}.
287: In the CSS $p_T$-resummation formalism~\cite{Collins:1984kg}, FO results are trustworthy when
288: $\alpha_s(Q^2)$ is perturbative, with $\Lambda_{\rm QCD} = 0.2\GeV$, and $q_T$ is comparable to $Q$:
289: \begin{equation}
290:  \log\frac{Q}{\Lambda_{\rm QCD}}\gg1 \quad\text{and}\quad \log^2\frac{Q}{q_T}\lesssim\log\frac{Q}{\Lambda_{\rm QCD}}.
291: \end{equation}
292: 
293: Imposing $Q = m_N$, jets in Eq.~(\ref{eq:qcdPowerSeries}) must satisfy
294: \begin{equation}
295:  \sum_k^n p_{T,k}^{j} \gtrsim m_N \times e^{-\sqrt{\log(m_N/\Lambda_{\rm QCD})}}.
296:  \label{eq:cssPTBound}
297: \end{equation}
298: Taking for example $n=1$ and $m_N$ up to $1~(1.5)\TeV$, the mass range of interest at 14 (100) TeV, this translates to
299: \begin{equation}
300:  p_T^j \gtrsim 55~(80)\GeV.
301: \end{equation}
302: Weaker $p_T^j$ cuts lead to artificially large logarithms and overestimated cross sections in Eq.~(\ref{eq:qcdPowerSeries}).
303: 
304: We cluster jets with FastJet~\cite{Cacciari:2005hq,Cacciari:2011ma} 
305: using the anti-$k_T$ algorithm~\cite{Cacciari:2008gp} with a separation parameter of $ \Delta R = 0.4$.
306: For differential events, we parton shower (PS) with Pythia 8.212~\cite{Sjostrand:2014zea}.
307: 
308: 
309: We equate the factorization and renormalization scales
310: to half the sum over final-state transverse masses (\texttt{dynamical\_scale\_choice=3} in \mgamc):
311: \begin{eqnarray}
312:  \mu_f, \mu_r, \mu_0 = \sum_{k=N,\ell,\text{jets}}\cfrac{m_{T,k}}{2} = \frac12\sum_{k} \sqrt{m_k^2 + p_{T,k}^2}.
313: \end{eqnarray}
314: 
315: 
316: 
317: 
318: 
319: 
320: We quantify the scale dependence by varying it over
321: \begin{equation}
322:  0.5  \leq \mu/ \mu_0 \leq2.
323: \end{equation}
324: 
325: 
326: In our framework, the CC DY rate at NLO can be calculated via the \mgamc~commands:
327: \begin{verbatim}
328: > import model HeavyN_NLO
329: > define p  = u c d s b u~ c~ d~ s~ b~ g

348: GF is a loop-induced process, which are only recently~\cite{Hirschi:2015iia} supported by \mgamc.
349: Such fully automated computations at NLO are unavailable since the two-loop technology does not currently exist.
350: We therefore perform the LO calculation matched and merged with up to one additional jet via the MLM scheme \cite{Mangano:2006rw}.
351: We discard loops that are actually virtual corrections to the DY process
352: and keep only diagrams where gluons do not appears in the loop.
353: The inclusive, unmatched LO GF rate can be calculated with
354:  \begin{verbatim}
355: > generate g g > n2 vv [QCD]
356: > output GGF_Nv_LO; launch;
357: \end{verbatim}

359: and the (anti-) symmetric nature of the residual $h~(Z)$ coupling~\cite{Willenbrock:1985tj,Hessler:2014ssa}.}

375: The difficulty in modeling $W\gamma$ fusion stems from the $t$-channel photon propagator, 
376: which, like Eq.~(\ref{eq:qcdPowerSeries}) for $N\ell^\pm+nj$, gives rise to logarithms of the form~\cite{Alva:2014gxa}
377: \begin{equation}
378: d\sigma(q_{1}q_{2}\rightarrow N \ell^\pm q_{1}' q_{2}') \sim 
379: \log\left(\cfrac{m_N^2}{M_W^2}\right)\log\left(\cfrac{m_N^2}{p_T^{j_\gamma 2}}\right).
380: \label{eq:VBFLogs}
381: \end{equation}
382: Here, $p_T^{j_\gamma}$ is the $p_T$ of the jet associated with the photon exchange.
383: However, consistent treatment of Eq.~(\ref{eq:VBFLogs}) dictates $p_T^j$ cuts excessive for $\gamma$-initiated processes. 
384: A resolution is to collinearly factorize and resum the photon piece into a DGLAP-evolved $\gamma$-PDF, consider instead
385: \begin{equation}
386:  q ~\gamma \rightarrow N ~\ell^\pm ~q',
387:  \label{eq:qaScattering}
388: \end{equation}
389: and evolve the PDF to the hard scattering scale.
390: One loses the ability to efficiently tag a second forward/backward jet but gains a large (logarithmic) total rate enhancement~\cite{Alva:2014gxa}.
391: Eq.~(\ref{eq:qaScattering}) is realization of the structure function approach to VBF~\cite{Han:1992hr}.
392: Formally, the $N\ell^\pm qq'$ channel can be recovered by performing the ACOT-like jet matching explicitly as in~\cite{Alva:2014gxa}
393: or evaluating the NLO in QED corrections to Eq.~(\ref{eq:qaScattering}).
394: For VBF, we impose the $\eta^{j},p_T^{j}$ cuts of~\cite{Alva:2014gxa}:
395: \begin{equation}
396:  \vert\eta^{j_\VBF}\vert < 4.5, \quad p_T^{j_\VBF} > 30\GeV.
397: \end{equation}
398: Collinear poles associated with $t$-channel $\ell$ exchange emerge in Eq.~(\ref{eq:qaScattering}) but are regulated by cuts in Eq.~(\ref{eq:LepCuts}).
399: The process at NLO in QCD is simulated by

402: > generate    q a > n2 mu q QED=3 QCD=0 [QCD]
403: > add process a q > n2 mu q QED=3 QCD=0 [QCD]
404: > output PP_VBF_NLO; launch;
405: \end{verbatim}

449: As a function of $m_N$, we present in Fig.~\ref{fig:xSec} the (a) 14 and (b) 100 TeV heavy $N$ production rates, divided by active-heavy mixing.
450: At NLO are the CC DY  (circle), NC DY (triangle), $N\ell^\pm+1j$ (diamond), and VBF (upside-down triangle) processes; at LO is GF (star).
451: The lower panel shows the NLO-to-LO ratio,
452: the so-called NLO $K$-factor:
453: \begin{equation}
454:  K^{NLO} \equiv \sigma^{\rm NLO} / \sigma^{\rm LO}.
455: \end{equation}
456: For select $m_N$, we summarize our results in Tb.~\ref{tb:xSec}.
457: 
458: For $m_N = 100-1000~(100-1500)\GeV$, NLO production rates for the DY channels at 14 (100) TeV span:
459: \begin{eqnarray}
460:  \DYCC	&:& {3.4\fb-16\pb	~\quad(25\fb-94\pb)},\\
461:  +1j	&:& {1.2\fb-2.1\pb	~\quad(12\fb-15\pb)},\\
462:  \DYNC	&:& {1.8\fb-23\pb	~\quad(16\fb-180\pb)},
463: \end{eqnarray}
464: with corresponding scale uncertainties:
465: \begin{eqnarray}
466:  \DYCC	&:& {\pm 1-5\%	~\quad(\pm1-11\%)},\\
467:  +1j	&:& {\pm 2-6\%	~\quad(\pm1-7\%)},\\
468:  \DYNC	&:& {\pm 1-5\%	~\quad(\pm1-13\%)},
469: \end{eqnarray}
470: and nearly identical $K$-factors:
471: \begin{eqnarray}
472: \DYCC, ~+1j, ~\text{NC} :\quad {1.15-1.25~(1.11-1.37)}.
473: \end{eqnarray}
474: The increase over LO rates is due to the opening of the $g\overset{(-)}{q}$  and $gg$ channels for the DY and $+1j$ processes, respectively.
475: Since the gluon PDF is largest at Bjorken-$x\sim m_N/\sqrt{s}\ll1$, the biggest change is at low $m_N$.
476: We find the that DY$+2j$ $K$-factors are consistent with high-mass SM DY in SHERPA~\cite{Gleisberg:2008ta}.
477: The modest size of these corrections validates our approach.
478: 
479: The VBF rate, uncertainty, and $K$-factor span
480: \begin{eqnarray}
481:  \sigma_{\VBF}			&:& {5.3-52\fb	~\quad(46-280\fb)},\\
482:  \delta\sigma_{\VBF}/\sigma	&:& {\pm5-11\%	~\quad(\pm9-14\%)},\\
483:  K_{\VBF} 			&:& {0.98-1.06	~\quad(0.90-0.96)}.
484: \end{eqnarray}
485: Due to collinear logarithmic enhancements, the VBF rate falls slower with $m_N$ than $s$-channel mechanisms.
486: At 14 (100) TeV, the VBF rate surpasses the CC DY rate at $m_N\approx {850~(1100)\GeV}.$
487: This somewhat differs from~\cite{Alva:2014gxa} and can be traced to the different $\gamma$-PDFs used:
488: at large (small) scales of $\tau = m_N^2/s$, the $q\gamma$ luminosity here is larger (smaller) than in~\cite{Alva:2014gxa},
489: leading to VBF overtaking the DY CC at smaller (larger) values of $m_N$.
490: However, present-day $\gamma$-PDF uncertainties are sizable~\cite{Ball:2013hta,Ababekri:2016kkj}. 
491: 
492: For all NLO processes, our scale dependence peaks at ${m_N = 100-200\GeV}$; 
493: it is attributed, in part, to the large gluon PDF uncertainty at small $x$.
494: 
495: For $m_N\geq 200\GeV$, the matched LO GF rate spans
496: \begin{eqnarray}
497:  \sigma_{\GF}	&:& {1.0\fb-0.1\pb	~\quad(55\fb-4.7\pb)}.
498: \end{eqnarray}
499: At 14 TeV, the rate is comparable to $N\ell+1j$ at NLO.
500: Though both obey $s$-channel scaling, the similarities are accidental and due to phase space cuts.
501: GF is roughly ${0.1-0.3\times}$ the CC DY rate.
502: At 100 TeV, the situation is qualitatively different:
503: Due to $gg$ luminosity increase at 100 TeV, which grows $\sim10\times$ more than the DY luminosity~\cite{Arkani-Hamed:2015vfh},
504: GF jumps to ${0.4-2\times}$ the CC DY rate, becoming the dominant  production mode for $m_N = {300-1500\GeV}$.
505: Beyond this $m_N$, VBF is largest. 
506: We observe that Higgs and $Z$ diagrams contribute about equally at large $m_N$.
507: Our matched results are consistent with the unmatched calculation of~\cite{Hessler:2014ssa}.

511: \subsection{NLO+PS Kinematics at 14 TeV}
512: We now consider the differential distribution for the processes in Fig.~\ref{fig:diagrams} but focus largely on the VBF channel.
513: 
514: The kinematics of heavy lepton production from DY currents at NLO and NLO+Leading Log(recoil) was studied in~\cite{Ruiz:2015zca}.
515: There, the differential NLO $K$-factors, defined as
516: \begin{equation}
517:  K_{\mathcal{O}}^{\rm NLO} \equiv \cfrac{d\sigma^{\rm NLO}/d\mathcal{O}}{d\sigma^{\rm LO}/d\mathcal{O}}
518: \end{equation}
519: for observable $\mathcal{O}$, were analytically shown to be flat in the leading regions of phase space.
520: In these regions, NLO contributions are dominated by soft initial-state radiation, which generically factorize for DY processes.
521: We confirm the flatness of $K_{\mathcal{O}}^{\rm NLOPS}$ for the DY channels, 
522: including for complex observables such as cluster mass in the $N\ell\rightarrow 3\ell \nu$ final state.
523: 
524: 
525: The phenomenology of the GF channel has not been previously studied.
526: It is beyond the scope of this investigation to do so here and will be presented elsewhere.
527: 
528: 
529: At $\sqrt{s} = 14$ TeV and representative  neutrino mass $m_N = 500\GeV$,
530: the LO distributions for the $W\gamma$ fusion process was studied in Ref.~\cite{Alva:2014gxa}.
531: 
532: For the first time, we show in Fig.~\ref{fig:vbfDifferential} the NLO+PS (dash) and LO+PS (solid)-accurate distributions with respect to 
533: (a,c) $p_T$ and (b,d) rapidity $(y)$ of the (a,b) $N$- and (c,d) $(N\ell)$-systems. $K_{\mathcal{O}}^{\rm NLOPS}$ is shown in the lower panel.
534: 
535: For the two system, but particularly the $(N\ell)$-system, we observe a net migration at NLOPS of events from the lowest $p_T$ bins
536: resulting in $K^{\rm NLOPS}_{p_T}<1$ for these bins. At high $p_T$, $K^{\rm NLOPS}_{p_T}$ quickly converges to unity from above.
537: 
538: In the rapidity distributions, we observe a similar, but more pronounced, migration of events from large $y$ to smaller values,
539: consistent with shifts to larger $p_T$.
540: 
541: The charged lepton $p_T$ and $\eta$ distributions (not shown) demonstrate little sensitivity to $\mathcal{O}(\alpha_s)$ corrections.
542: However, as VBF is dominated by $\gamma\rightarrow \ell$ splittings~\cite{Alva:2014gxa}, 
543: one does not expect such sensitivity to QCD radiation until $\mathcal{O}(\alpha^2 \alpha_s)$.
544: 
545: Though numerically less significant, we find that the NLO corrections to the VBF distributions are qualitatively different than those of DY-like systems:
546: whereas differential $K$-factors for DY processes tend to remain flat and above unity,
547: QCD corrections for $W\gamma$ fusion tend to depopulate low-$p_T$/forward regions of phase space and populate high-$p_T$/central regions.
548: This results in $K$-factors both above and below unity.

568: \section{Summary and Conclusion}\label{sec:Conclusions}
569: 
570: The origin of light neutrino masses remains elusive.
571: Extended neutrino mass models predict the existence TeV-scale heavy neutrinos $N_i$ that may be discovered at current or future collider experiments.
572: 
573: We propose a systematic treatment of $N$ production mechanisms at hadron colliders, 
574: and provide instructions for building IRC-safe VBF and $N\ell^\pm+nj$ signal definitions.
575: The prescription remedies issues that have plagued past analyses,
576: and is applicable to a number of other SM and BSM processes.
577: We report modest NLO corrections, demonstrating the perturbative stability of our approach.
578: 
579: We present also the first NLOPS-accurate differential distributions for the $W\gamma$ VBF process.
580: We observe nontrivial differential $K$-factors below and above unity.
581: 
582: In a model-independent fashion,
583: we present for the first time a comparison of all leading single $N$ production modes at $\sqrt{s} = 14$ and $100$ TeV.
584: Fully differential results up to NLO in QCD accuracy are obtained through a MC tool chain linking FeynRules, \nloct, and \mgamc.
585: 
586: Associated model files are publicly available~\cite{nloFRModel}.

1: (***************************************************************************************************************)
2: (******                       This is the FeynRules mod-file for the Standard model                       ******)
3: (******                                                                                                   ******)
4: (******     Authors: N. Christensen, C. Duhr, B. Fuks                                                     ******)
5: (******                                                                                                   ******)
6: (****** Choose whether Feynman gauge is desired.                                                          ******)
7: (****** If set to False, unitary gauge is assumed.                                                          ****)
8: (****** Feynman gauge is especially useful for CalcHEP/CompHEP where the calculation is 10-100 times faster. ***)
9: (****** Feynman gauge is not supported in MadGraph and Sherpa.                                              ****)
10: (***************************************************************************************************************)
11: 
12: (* ************************** *)
13: (* *****  Information   ***** *)
14: (* ************************** *)
15: M$ModelName = "Standard Model";
16: 
17: M$Information = {
18:   Authors      -> {"N. Christensen", "C. Duhr", "B. Fuks"}, 
19:   Version      -> "1.4.7",
20:   Date         -> "28. 09. 2016",
21:   Institutions -> {"Michigan State University", "Universite catholique de Louvain (CP3)", "IPHC Strasbourg / University of Strasbourg"},
22:   Emails       -> {"neil@pa.msu.edu", "claude.duhr@uclouvain.be", "benjamin.fuks@cnrs.in2p3.fr"},
23:   URLs         -> "http://feynrules.phys.ucl.ac.be/view/Main/StandardModel"
24: };
25: 
26: FeynmanGauge = True;
27: 
28: (* ************************** *)
29: (* ***** NLO Variables ****** *)
30: (******************************)
31: 
32: FR$LoopSwitches = {{Gf, MW}};
33: FR$RmDblExt = { ymb -> MB, ymc -> MC, ymdo -> MD, yme -> Me, 
34:    ymm -> MMU, yms -> MS, ymt -> MT, ymtau -> MTA, ymup -> MU};
35: 
36: (* ************************** *)
37: (* *****  Change  log   ***** *)
38: (* ************************** *)
39: 
40: (* v1.4.7: Index issue with the ghost Lagrangian (special thanks to S. Iwamoto *)
41: (* v1.4.6: NLO variable added.                                               *)
42: (* v1.4.5: Added widths for ghosts.                                          *)
43: (* v1.4.4: Changed widths of goldstone bosons to be the same as for the W and Z bosons *)
44: (* v1.4.3: Updated conventions for the symmetric structure constants of SU3. *)
45: (* v1.4.2: Set FeynmanGauge=True as default again.                           *)
46: (* v1.4: Added SU(2) representation.                                         *)
47: (*       -> Modification in the field declarations (doublets are added)      *)
48: (*       -> Modification in the Lagrangian (much simpler).                   *)
49: (* v1.3: Added yukawa couplings for all fermions for gauge invariance.       *)
50: (*       Added yukawa couplings for 1st generation fermions to Massless.rst. *)
51: (*       Updated parameters to PDG 2010.                                     *)
52: (* v1.2: Set FeynmanGauge=True as default.                                   *)
53: (*       Set Gluonic ghosts to be included in both gauges.                   *)
54: (* v1.1: Fixed yukawa couplings in Feynman gauge.                            *)
55: (*       Changed yd[n] CKM[n,m] to yd[m] CKM[n,m].                           *)
56: (*       Changed yu[n] Conjugate[CKM[m,n]] to yu[m] Conjugate[CKM[m,n]].     *)
57: 
58: (* ************************** *)
59: (* *****      vevs      ***** *)
60: (* ************************** *)
61: M$vevs = { {Phi[2],vev} };
62: 
63: (* ************************** *)
64: (* *****  Gauge groups  ***** *)
65: (* ************************** *)
66: M$GaugeGroups = {
67:   U1Y  == { 
68:     Abelian          -> True,  
69:     CouplingConstant -> g1, 
70:     GaugeBoson       -> B, 
71:     Charge           -> Y
72:   },
73:   SU2L == { 
74:     Abelian           -> False, 
75:     CouplingConstant  -> gw, 
76:     GaugeBoson        -> Wi, 
77:     StructureConstant -> Eps, 
78:     Representations   -> {Ta,SU2D}, 
79:     Definitions       -> {Ta[a_,b_,c_]->PauliSigma[a,b,c]/2, FSU2L[i_,j_,k_]:> I Eps[i,j,k]}
80:   },
81:   SU3C == { 
82:     Abelian           -> False, 
83:     CouplingConstant  -> gs, 
84:     GaugeBoson        -> G,
85:     StructureConstant -> f, 
86:     Representations   -> {T,Colour}, 
87:     SymmetricTensor   -> dSUN
88:   } 
89: };
90: 
91: 
92: (* ************************** *)
93: (* *****    Indices     ***** *)
94: (* ************************** *)
95: 
96: IndexRange[Index[SU2W      ]] = Unfold[Range[3]]; 
97: IndexRange[Index[SU2D      ]] = Unfold[Range[2]];
98: IndexRange[Index[Gluon     ]] = NoUnfold[Range[8]];
99: IndexRange[Index[Colour    ]] = NoUnfold[Range[3]]; 
100: IndexRange[Index[Generation]] = Range[3];

102: IndexStyle[SU2W,       j];
103: IndexStyle[SU2D,       k];
104: IndexStyle[Gluon,      a];
105: IndexStyle[Colour,     m];
106: IndexStyle[Generation, f];

695: LGauge := Block[{mu,nu,ii,aa}, 
696:   ExpandIndices[-1/4 FS[B,mu,nu] FS[B,mu,nu] - 1/4 FS[Wi,mu,nu,ii] FS[Wi,mu,nu,ii] - 1/4 FS[G,mu,nu,aa] FS[G,mu,nu,aa], FlavorExpand->SU2W]];
697: 
698: LFermions := Block[{mu}, 
699:   ExpandIndices[I*(
700:     QLbar.Ga[mu].DC[QL, mu] + LLbar.Ga[mu].DC[LL, mu] + uRbar.Ga[mu].DC[uR, mu] + dRbar.Ga[mu].DC[dR, mu] + lRbar.Ga[mu].DC[lR, mu]), 
701:   FlavorExpand->{SU2W,SU2D}]/.{CKM[a_,b_] Conjugate[CKM[a_,c_]]->IndexDelta[b,c], CKM[b_,a_] Conjugate[CKM[c_,a_]]->IndexDelta[b,c]}];
702: 
703: LHiggs := Block[{ii,mu, feynmangaugerules},
704:   feynmangaugerules = If[Not[FeynmanGauge], {G0|GP|GPbar ->0}, {}];
705:  
706:   ExpandIndices[DC[Phibar[ii],mu] DC[Phi[ii],mu] + muH^2 Phibar[ii] Phi[ii] - lam Phibar[ii] Phi[ii] Phibar[jj] Phi[jj], FlavorExpand->{SU2D,SU2W}]/.feynmangaugerules
707:  ];
708: 
709: LYukawa := Block[{sp,ii,jj,cc,ff1,ff2,ff3,yuk,feynmangaugerules},
710:   feynmangaugerules = If[Not[FeynmanGauge], {G0|GP|GPbar ->0}, {}];
711:  
712:   yuk = ExpandIndices[
713:    -yd[ff2, ff3] CKM[ff1, ff2] QLbar[sp, ii, ff1, cc].dR [sp, ff3, cc] Phi[ii] - 
714:     yl[ff1, ff3] LLbar[sp, ii, ff1].lR [sp, ff3] Phi[ii] - 
715:     yu[ff1, ff2] QLbar[sp, ii, ff1, cc].uR [sp, ff2, cc] Phibar[jj] Eps[ii, jj], FlavorExpand -> SU2D];
716:   yuk = yuk /. { CKM[a_, b_] Conjugate[CKM[a_, c_]] -> IndexDelta[b, c], CKM[b_, a_] Conjugate[CKM[c_, a_]] -> IndexDelta[b, c]};
717:   yuk+HC[yuk]/.feynmangaugerules
718:  ];
719: 
720: LGhost := Block[{LGh1,LGhw,LGhs,LGhphi,mu, generators,gh,ghbar,Vectorize,phi1,phi2,togoldstones,doublet,doublet0},
721:   (* Pure gauge piece *) 	
722:   LGh1 = -ghBbar.del[DC[ghB,mu],mu];
723:   LGhw = -ghWibar[ii].del[DC[ghWi[ii],mu],mu];
724:   LGhs = -ghGbar[ii].del[DC[ghG[ii],mu],mu];
725: 
726:   (* Scalar pieces: see Peskin pages 739-742 *)
727:   (* phi1 and phi2 are the real degrees of freedom of GP *)
728:   (* Vectorize transforms a doublet in a vector in the phi-basis, i.e. the basis of real degrees of freedom *)
729:   gh    = {ghB, ghWi[1], ghWi[2], ghWi[3]};
730:   ghbar = {ghBbar, ghWibar[1], ghWibar[2], ghWibar[3]};
731:   generators = {-I/2 g1 IdentityMatrix[2], -I/2 gw PauliSigma[1], -I/2 gw PauliSigma[2], -I/2 gw PauliSigma[3]};
732:   doublet = Expand[{(-I phi1 - phi2)/Sqrt[2], Phi[2]} /. MR$Definitions /. vev -> 0]; 
733:   doublet0 = {0, vev/Sqrt[2]};
734:   Vectorize[{a_, b_}]:= Simplify[{Sqrt[2] Re[Expand[a]], Sqrt[2] Im[Expand[a]], Sqrt[2] Re[Expand[b]], Sqrt[2] Im[Expand[b]]}/.{Im[_]->0, Re[num_]->num}];
735:   togoldstones := {phi1 -> (GP + GPbar)/Sqrt[2], phi2 -> (-GP + GPbar)/(I Sqrt[2])};
736:   LGhphi=Plus@@Flatten[Table[-ghbar[[kkk]].gh[[lll]] Vectorize[generators[[kkk]].doublet0].Vectorize[generators[[lll]].(doublet+doublet0)],{kkk,4},{lll,4}]] /.togoldstones;
737: 
738: ExpandIndices[ LGhs + If[FeynmanGauge, LGh1 + LGhw + LGhphi,0], FlavorExpand->SU2W]];

(* ***** NLO Variables ****** *)

FR$LoopSwitches = {{Gf, MW}};

(* v1.4.5: Added widths for ghosts.                                          *)
(* v1.4.4: Changed widths of goldstone bosons to be the same as for the W and Z bosons *)
(* v1.4.3: Updated conventions for the symmetric structure constants of SU3. *)
(* v1.4.2: Set FeynmanGauge=True as default again.                           *)
(* v1.4: Added SU(2) representation.                                         *)
(*       -> Modification in the field declarations (doublets are added)      *)
(*       -> Modification in the Lagrangian (much simpler).                   *)
(* v1.3: Added yukawa couplings for all fermions for gauge invariance.       *)
(*       Added yukawa couplings for 1st generation fermions to Massless.rst. *)
(*       Updated parameters to PDG 2010.                                     *)
(* v1.2: Set FeynmanGauge=True as default.                                   *)
(*       Set Gluonic ghosts to be included in both gauges.                   *)
(* v1.1: Fixed yukawa couplings in Feynman gauge.                            *)
(*       Changed yd[n] CKM[n,m] to yd[m] CKM[n,m].                           *)
(*       Changed yu[n] Conjugate[CKM[m,n]] to yu[m] Conjugate[CKM[m,n]].     *)

    StructureConstant -> f, 
    Representations   -> {T,Colour},

    TeX              -> Superscript[y, u],
    Description      -> "Up-type Yukawa couplings"
  },
  yd == {
    ParameterType    -> Internal,
    Indices          -> {Index[Generation], Index[Generation]},
    Definitions      -> {yd[i_?NumericQ, j_?NumericQ] :> 0  /; (i =!= j)},
    Value            -> {yd[1,1] -> Sqrt[2] ymdo/vev, yd[2,2] -> Sqrt[2] yms/vev, yd[3,3] -> Sqrt[2] ymb/vev},
    InteractionOrder -> {QED, 1},
    ParameterName    -> {yd[1,1] -> ydo, yd[2,2] -> ys, yd[3,3] -> yb},
    TeX              -> Superscript[y, d],
    Description      -> "Down-type Yukawa couplings"
  },
(* N. B. : only Cabibbo mixing! *)
  CKM == { 
    ParameterType -> Internal,
    Indices       -> {Index[Generation], Index[Generation]},
    Unitary       -> True,
    Value         -> {CKM[1,1] -> Cos[cabi],  CKM[1,2] -> Sin[cabi], CKM[1,3] -> 0,
                      CKM[2,1] -> -Sin[cabi], CKM[2,2] -> Cos[cabi], CKM[2,3] -> 0,
                      CKM[3,1] -> 0,          CKM[3,2] -> 0,         CKM[3,3] -> 1},
    TeX         -> Superscript[V,CKM],
    Description -> "CKM-Matrix"}
};

(* ************************** *)
(* *****   Lagrangian   ***** *)
(* ************************** *)

LGauge := Block[{mu,nu,ii,aa}, 
  ExpandIndices[-1/4 FS[B,mu,nu] FS[B,mu,nu] - 1/4 FS[Wi,mu,nu,ii] FS[Wi,mu,nu,ii] - 1/4 FS[G,mu,nu,aa] FS[G,mu,nu,aa], FlavorExpand->SU2W]];

LFermions := Block[{mu}, 
  ExpandIndices[I*(
    QLbar.Ga[mu].DC[QL, mu] + LLbar.Ga[mu].DC[LL, mu] + uRbar.Ga[mu].DC[uR, mu] + dRbar.Ga[mu].DC[dR, mu] + lRbar.Ga[mu].DC[lR, mu]), 
  FlavorExpand->{SU2W,SU2D}]/.{CKM[a_,b_] Conjugate[CKM[a_,c_]]->IndexDelta[b,c], CKM[b_,a_] Conjugate[CKM[c_,a_]]->IndexDelta[b,c]}];

LHiggs := Block[{ii,mu, feynmangaugerules},
  feynmangaugerules = If[Not[FeynmanGauge], {G0|GP|GPbar ->0}, {}];
 
  ExpandIndices[DC[Phibar[ii],mu] DC[Phi[ii],mu] + muH^2 Phibar[ii] Phi[ii] - lam Phibar[ii] Phi[ii] Phibar[jj] Phi[jj], FlavorExpand->{SU2D,SU2W}]/.feynmangaugerules
 ];

LYukawa := Block[{sp,ii,jj,cc,ff1,ff2,ff3,yuk,feynmangaugerules},
  feynmangaugerules = If[Not[FeynmanGauge], {G0|GP|GPbar ->0}, {}];
 
  yuk = ExpandIndices[
   -yd[ff2, ff3] CKM[ff1, ff2] QLbar[sp, ii, ff1, cc].dR [sp, ff3, cc] Phi[ii] - 
    yl[ff1, ff3] LLbar[sp, ii, ff1].lR [sp, ff3] Phi[ii] - 
    yu[ff1, ff2] QLbar[sp, ii, ff1, cc].uR [sp, ff2, cc] Phibar[jj] Eps[ii, jj], FlavorExpand -> SU2D];
  yuk = yuk /. { CKM[a_, b_] Conjugate[CKM[a_, c_]] -> IndexDelta[b, c], CKM[b_, a_] Conjugate[CKM[c_, a_]] -> IndexDelta[b, c]};
  yuk+HC[yuk]/.feynmangaugerules
 ];

LGhost := Block[{LGh1,LGhw,LGhs,LGhphi,mu, generators,gh,ghbar,Vectorize,phi1,phi2,togoldstones,doublet,doublet0},
  (* Pure gauge piece *) 	
  LGh1 = -ghBbar.del[DC[ghB,mu],mu];
  LGhw = -ghWibar[ii].del[DC[ghWi[ii],mu],mu];
  LGhs = -ghGbar[ii].del[DC[ghG[ii],mu],mu];

  (* Scalar pieces: see Peskin pages 739-742 *)
  (* phi1 and phi2 are the real degrees of freedom of GP *)
  (* Vectorize transforms a doublet in a vector in the phi-basis, i.e. the basis of real degrees of freedom *)
  gh    = {ghB, ghWi[1], ghWi[2], ghWi[3]};
  ghbar = {ghBbar, ghWibar[1], ghWibar[2], ghWibar[3]};
  generators = {-I/2 g1 IdentityMatrix[2], -I/2 gw PauliSigma[1], -I/2 gw PauliSigma[2], -I/2 gw PauliSigma[3]};
  doublet = Expand[{(-I phi1 - phi2)/Sqrt[2], Phi[2]} /. MR$Definitions /. vev -> 0]; 
  doublet0 = {0, vev/Sqrt[2]};
  Vectorize[{a_, b_}]:= Simplify[{Sqrt[2] Re[Expand[a]], Sqrt[2] Im[Expand[a]], Sqrt[2] Re[Expand[b]], Sqrt[2] Im[Expand[b]]}/.{Im[_]->0, Re[num_]->num}];
  togoldstones := {phi1 -> (GP + GPbar)/Sqrt[2], phi2 -> (-GP + GPbar)/(I Sqrt[2])};
  LGhphi=Plus@@Flatten[Table[-ghbar[[kkk]].gh[[lll]] Vectorize[generators[[kkk]].doublet0].Vectorize[generators[[lll]].(doublet+doublet0)],{kkk,4},{lll,4}]] /.togoldstones;

ExpandIndices[ LGhs + If[FeynmanGauge, LGh1 + LGhw + LGhphi,0], FlavorExpand->SU2W]];

LSM:= LGauge + LFermions + LHiggs + LYukawa + LGhost;

1: #!/usr/bin/env python3
2: """Deterministic lints for an agent-written FeynRules add-on (.fr) file.
3: 
4: Every rule encodes one construct that broke a compile, a FeynRules check or a
5: MadGraph import in the benchmark (prompt_addendum_v3.txt rules 9-15 and the
6: repair-loop taxonomy). A lint runs in milliseconds on the text; the compile it
7: predicts takes up to 900 s.
8: 
9: Each finding carries the STAGE it predicts:
10:   compile  - FeynRules will not load or will not finish the model
11:   checks   - the model loads but a consistency check fails
12:   mg5      - the UFO is written but MadGraph rejects it
13:   harness  - the validation harness cannot pick the total Lagrangian
14:   warn     - FeynRules warns; the run may still pass
15: 
16: Library: ``lint_text(text) -> list[Finding]``. CLI: ``fr_lint.py file.fr``.
17: """
18: 
19: from __future__ import annotations
20: 
21: import json
22: import re
23: import sys
24: from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
25: from pathlib import Path
26: from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Set
27: 
28: HEPTAPOD = Path.home() / "Documents/Github/heptapod"
29: SM_FR = HEPTAPOD / "tools/feynrules/test_files/models/SM.fr"
30: 
31: # Mathematica built-ins and FeynRules symbols a class, parameter or index must
32: # not be named after (rule 10).
33: FR_SYMBOLS = {"HC", "CC", "FS", "DC", "del", "Eps", "Ga", "ProjP", "ProjM", "T",
34:               "Sig", "PauliSigma", "IndexDelta", "ME", "Index", "Indices", "Mass",
35:               "Width", "Value", "Unphysical", "Abelian"}
36: PROTECTED = {"N", "C", "D", "E", "I", "K", "O", "Pi", "Gamma", "Beta", "Zeta",
37:              "Sqrt", "Exp", "Log", "Sin", "Cos", "Tan", "Re", "Im", "Conjugate",
38:              "Sum", "Block", "Module", "Table", "If", "Which"}
39: 
40: # Names SM.fr declares: classes, class members, parameters, gauge groups, indices.
41: _SM_TEXT = SM_FR.read_text() if SM_FR.is_file() else ""
42: SM_CLASSES: Set[str] = set(re.findall(r"ClassName\s*->\s*(\w+)", _SM_TEXT))
43: SM_MEMBERS: Set[str] = set()
44: for _m in re.findall(r"ClassMembers\s*->\s*\{([^}]*)\}", _SM_TEXT):
45:     SM_MEMBERS |= {x.strip() for x in _m.split(",") if x.strip()}
46: _i = _SM_TEXT.find("M$Parameters")
47: SM_PARAMS: Set[str] = set(re.findall(r"^\s*(\w+)\s*==\s*\{", _SM_TEXT[_i:], re.M)) if _i >= 0 else set()
48: SM_GAUGE = {"U1Y", "SU2L", "SU3C"}
49: SM_INDICES = {"Generation", "Colour", "Gluon", "SU2D", "SU2W", "Lorentz", "Spin",
50:               "Spin1", "Spin2", "Sextet"}
51: SM_FIELDS_ALL = SM_CLASSES | SM_MEMBERS | {c + "bar" for c in SM_CLASSES | SM_MEMBERS}
52: SM_MASSES = {"MZ", "MW", "MH", "Me", "MMU", "MTA", "MU", "MC", "MT", "MD", "MS", "MB",
53:              "WZ", "WW", "WH", "WT"}
54: 
55: FR_BUILTINS = {"HC", "CC", "FS", "DC", "del", "Eps", "Ga", "ProjP", "ProjM", "T",
56:                "PauliSigma", "IndexDelta", "ME", "Sqrt", "Exp", "Log", "Sin", "Cos",
57:                "Tan", "I", "Pi", "Sum", "Block", "Module", "ExpandIndices",
58:                "FlavorExpand", "True", "False", "bar", "anti", "left", "right",
59:                "Conjugate", "Re", "Im", "Abs", "Sig", "Ta", "T6", "K6", "K6bar",
60:                "K3", "K3bar", "f", "dSUN", "Dot", "Times", "Plus", "Power",
61:                "Automatic", "Internal", "External", "Unfold", "NoUnfold", "Range",
62:                "Index", "Lorentz", "Spin", "Colour", "Gluon", "Generation",
63:                "SU2D", "SU2W", "Sextet", "IndexStyle", "MakeIdenticalFermions",
64:                "Expand", "Simplify", "ProjPlus", "ProjMinus", "FR$", "vev"}
65: 
66: 
67: @dataclass
68: class Finding:
69:     rule: str
70:     stage: str  # compile | checks | mg5 | harness | warn
71:     message: str
72:     line: Optional[int] = None
73: 
74: 
75: # ------------------------------------------------------------------ parsing
76: 
77: def strip_comments(text: str) -> str:
78:     out, depth, i = [], 0, 0
79:     while i < len(text):
80:         if text.startswith("(*", i):
81:             depth += 1
82:             i += 2
83:             continue
84:         if text.startswith("*)", i) and depth:
85:             depth -= 1
86:             i += 2
87:             continue
88:         if depth == 0:
89:             out.append(text[i])
90:         elif text[i] == "\n":
91:             out.append("\n")
92:         i += 1
93:     return "".join(out)
94: 
95: 
96: def _matching(text: str, open_idx: int) -> int:
97:     depth = 0
98:     pairs = {"{": "}", "[": "]", "(": ")"}
99:     closes = set(pairs.values())
100:     for j in range(open_idx, len(text)):
101:         ch = text[j]
102:         if ch in pairs:
103:             depth += 1
104:         elif ch in closes:
105:             depth -= 1
106:             if depth == 0:
107:                 return j
108:     return len(text) - 1
109: 
110: 
111: def _block(text: str, name: str) -> str:
112:     m = re.search(rf"M\${name}\s*=\s*\{{", text)
113:     if not m:
114:         return ""
115:     end = _matching(text, m.end() - 1)
116:     return text[m.end():end]
117: 
118: 
119: def _entries(block: str) -> List[Dict]:
120:     """Top-level `Head == { ... }` entries of a M$ block."""
121:     out = []
122:     for m in re.finditer(r"(\w+(?:\[\s*\d+\s*\])?)\s*==\s*\{", block):
123:         end = _matching(block, m.end() - 1)
124:         body = block[m.end():end]
125:         out.append({"head": m.group(1), "body": body, "pos": m.start()})
126:     return out
127: 
128: 
129: def _prop(body: str, key: str) -> Optional[str]:
130:     m = re.search(rf"\b{key}\s*->\s*", body)
131:     if not m:
132:         return None
133:     rest = body[m.end():]
134:     if rest.startswith("{"):
135:         return rest[: _matching(rest, 0) + 1]
136:     mm = re.match(r"[^,}\n]+", rest)
137:     return mm.group(0).strip() if mm else None
138: 
139: 
140: def _is_kin_name(name: str) -> bool:
141:     return bool(re.search(r"kin|Kin|KIN|free|Free|Gauge|gauge", name))
142: 
143: 
144: def term_defs(text: str) -> List[Dict]:
145:     starts = [(m.group(1), m.start()) for m in re.finditer(r"^(L\w+)\s*:?=", text, re.M)]
146:     stops = [m.start() for m in re.finditer(r"^(?:M\$\w+\s*=|L\w+\s*:?=|\w+\s*=\s*\{)", text, re.M)]
147:     out = []
148:     for name, s in starts:
149:         e = min([x for x in stops if x > s] + [len(text)])
150:         out.append({"name": name, "body": text[s:e], "line": text[:s].count("\n") + 1})
151:     return out
152: 
153: 
154: def _line_of(text: str, needle: str) -> Optional[int]:
155:     i = text.find(needle)
156:     return text[:i].count("\n") + 1 if i >= 0 else None
157: 
158: 
159: # -------------------------------------------------------------------- lints
160: 
161: def lint_text(raw: str) -> List[Finding]:
162:     text = strip_comments(raw)
163:     F: List[Finding] = []
164:     classes = _entries(_block(text, "ClassesDescription"))
165:     params = _entries(_block(text, "Parameters"))
166:     terms = term_defs(text)
167:     term_names = {t["name"] for t in terms}
168:     term_bodies = "\n".join(t["body"] for t in terms)
169: 
170:     class_names, class_idx = {}, {}
171:     for c in classes:
172:         cn = _prop(c["body"], "ClassName")
173:         if cn:
174:             class_names[cn] = c
175:             mi = re.match(r"(\w+)\[\s*(\d+)\s*\]", c["head"])
176:             if mi:
177:                 class_idx[cn] = (mi.group(1), int(mi.group(2)))
178:     param_names = {p["head"]: p for p in params}
179:     index_decls = dict(re.findall(r"IndexRange\[\s*Index\[(\w+)\]\s*\]\s*=\s*([^;\n]+)", text))
180: 
181:     # --- rule 10: names -------------------------------------------------
182:     for name in list(class_names) + list(param_names) + list(index_decls):
183:         if name in FR_SYMBOLS:
184:             F.append(Finding("feynrules_symbol_name", "compile",
185:                              f"`{name}` is a FeynRules symbol", _line_of(text, name)))
186:         elif name in PROTECTED:
187:             F.append(Finding("protected_name", "warn",
188:                              f"`{name}` is a Mathematica built-in (loads with a warning; renaming is safer)",
189:                              _line_of(text, name)))
190:     for name in class_names:
191:         if name in SM_CLASSES or name in SM_MEMBERS:
192:             F.append(Finding("sm_class_redeclared", "warn",
193:                              f"class `{name}` is already declared by SM.fr (doubly-defined class)",
194:                              _line_of(text, f"ClassName -> {name}")))
195:     for name in param_names:
196:         if name in SM_PARAMS or name in SM_MASSES:
197:             F.append(Finding("sm_parameter_redeclared", "warn",
198:                              f"parameter `{name}` is already declared by SM.fr", _line_of(text, name)))
199:     for cn, c in class_names.items():
200:         for key in ("ParticleName", "AntiParticleName"):
201:             v = _prop(c["body"], key)
202:             names = re.findall(r'"([^"]*)"', v) if v else []
203:             if v and any(re.search(r"[\'`\s!@#%^&*()=\[\]{}|\\;:<>?/,]", nm) for nm in names):
204:                 F.append(Finding("bad_particle_name", "mg5",
205:                                  f"class `{cn}`: {key} {v} is not a valid UFO identifier", _line_of(text, v)))
206:         if cn in class_idx and class_idx[cn][1] < 100:
207:             F.append(Finding("low_class_index", "warn",
208:                              f"class `{cn}` uses index {class_idx[cn][0]}[{class_idx[cn][1]}]; SM.fr uses the low indices",
209:                              _line_of(text, c["head"])))
210:         for m in re.finditer(r"ClassMembers\s*->\s*\{([^}]*)\}", c["body"]):
211:             for mem in [x.strip() for x in m.group(1).split(",") if x.strip()]:
212:                 if mem in SM_MEMBERS or mem in SM_CLASSES:
213:                     F.append(Finding("sm_member_redeclared", "compile",
214:                                      f"class member `{mem}` of `{cn}` collides with an SM.fr name",
215:                                      _line_of(text, mem)))
216:     if "$" in re.sub(r"M\$\w+", "", text):
217:         for m in re.finditer(r"\b\w*\$\w*", text):
218:             if not re.match(r"^(M|MR|FR)\$", m.group(0)):
219:                 F.append(Finding("dollar_in_name", "mg5", f"`{m.group(0)}` contains `$` (invalid Python)",
220:                                  text[:m.start()].count("\n") + 1))
221:                 break
222: 
223:     # --- rule 11: interaction orders --------------------------------------
224:     hierarchy = _block(text, "InteractionOrderHierarchy")
225:     orders_declared = set(re.findall(r"\{\s*(\w+)\s*,\s*-?\d+\s*\}", hierarchy))
226:     for pn, p in param_names.items():
227:         body = p["body"]
228:         ptype = (_prop(body, "ParameterType") or "External").strip()
229:         io = _prop(body, "InteractionOrder")
230:         used = re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(pn)}\b", term_bodies) is not None
231:         is_mass = any(re.search(rf"Mass\s*->\s*\{{\s*{re.escape(pn)}\b", c["body"]) or
232:                       re.search(rf"Width\s*->\s*\{{\s*{re.escape(pn)}\b", c["body"])
233:                       for c in classes) or re.match(r"^(M|W)[A-Z]", pn) and not io
234:         if io:
235:             oname = re.findall(r"\{\s*(\w+)\s*,", io)
236:             for o in oname:
237:                 if o not in orders_declared and o not in ("QCD", "QED"):
238:                     F.append(Finding("order_not_in_hierarchy", "warn",
239:                                      f"parameter `{pn}` uses InteractionOrder `{o}` not listed in M$InteractionOrderHierarchy",
240:                                      _line_of(text, pn)))
241:     ordered = {pn for pn, p in param_names.items() if _prop(p["body"], "InteractionOrder")}
242:     internal = {pn for pn, p in param_names.items()
243:                 if (_prop(p["body"], "ParameterType") or "External").strip() == "Internal"}
244:     # an Internal parameter inherits the orders of the parameters in its Value
245:     for pn in list(internal):
246:         val = _prop(param_names[pn]["body"], "Value") or ""
247:         if any(re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(o)}\b", val) for o in ordered):
248:             ordered.add(pn)
249:     for t in terms:
250:         if _is_kin_name(t["name"]):
251:             continue
252:         used_params = {pn for pn in param_names if re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(pn)}\b", t["body"])}
253:         sm_couplings = {"ee", "gw", "gs", "g1", "yl", "yu", "yd", "lam", "CKM"}
254:         if used_params and not (used_params & ordered) and not \
255:                 any(re.search(rf"\b{c}\b", t["body"]) for c in sm_couplings) and \
256:                 not any(re.search(rf"\b(DC|FS)\[", t["body"]) for _ in [0]):
257:             F.append(Finding("missing_interaction_order", "mg5",
258:                              f"`{t['name']}`: none of its parameters ({', '.join(sorted(used_params))}) carries an InteractionOrder",
259:                              t["line"]))
260: 
261:     # --- rule 12: pattern rules on tensor parameters -----------------------
262:     for pn, p in param_names.items():
263:         if re.search(r"\w+\[[^\]]*_[^\]]*\]\s*:?->", p["body"]) or "_?NumericQ" in p["body"]:
264:             F.append(Finding("pattern_rule_definition", "mg5",
265:                              f"parameter `{pn}` uses a pattern rule in Definitions/Value; FeynRules exports it verbatim as a UFO name",
266:                              _line_of(text, pn)))
267:     for cn, c in class_names.items():
268:         d = _prop(c["body"], "Definitions") or ""
269:         if re.search(r"\w+\[[^\]]*_[^\]]*\]\s*:>", d) and not re.search(r"\w+\[[^\]]*_\s*[,\]]", d):
270:             pass  # `X[mu_] :> ...` is the normal FeynRules idiom; leave it
271: 
272:     # --- rule 13: explicit indices ------------------------------------------
273:     for t in terms:
274:         b = t["body"]
275:         for m in re.finditer(r"DC\[\s*(\w+)\[([^\]]*)\]\s*,", b):
276:             fld = m.group(1)
277:             c = class_names.get(fld)
278:             idx = (_prop(c["body"], "Indices") or "") if c else ""
279:             if c and re.search(r"Colour|Sextet|Gluon|Octet|Col", idx):
280:                 F.append(Finding("explicit_index_in_dc", "compile",
281:                                  f"`{t['name']}`: covariant derivative on `{fld}` with an explicit colour-type index", t["line"]))
282:             else:
283:                 F.append(Finding("explicit_index_in_dc", "warn",
284:                                  f"`{t['name']}`: covariant derivative on an explicitly indexed field `{fld}`", t["line"]))
285:             break
286:         if re.search(r"Index\[\s*Generation\s*,\s*\w+\s*\]\s*,\s*Index\[\s*Generation", b) or \
287:                 re.search(r"\w+\[\s*Generation\s*,\s*\w+\s*\]", b):
288:             F.append(Finding("nested_generation_index", "compile",
289:                              f"`{t['name']}`: nested generation index", t["line"]))
290:         m = re.search(r"\b(\w+)\[\s*(ff\d?|gen\d?|ii\d?)\s*,\s*(ff\d?|gen\d?|jj\d?)\s*\]\s*\w+bar\[", b)
291:         if m and m.group(1) in param_names:
292:             F.append(Finding("explicit_flavour_sum", "mg5",
293:                              f"`{t['name']}`: flavour matrix `{m.group(1)}` with explicit generation indices instead of matrix form",
294:                              t["line"]))
295: 
296:     # --- rule 14: one declared total ---------------------------------------
297:     roots = []
298:     for t in terms:
299:         if not any(re.search(rf"\b{t['name']}\b", u["body"]) for u in terms if u is not t):
300:             roots.append(t["name"])
301:     if terms and not roots:
302:         F.append(Finding("no_total_lagrangian", "harness", "no Lagrangian symbol is a root (circular or empty)", None))
303:     elif len(roots) > 1:
304:         F.append(Finding("ambiguous_total", "harness",
305:                          f"{len(roots)} root Lagrangian symbols: {', '.join(roots)}", None))
306:     elif roots and roots[0] not in ("LTotal", "LTot", "LFull", "LBSM", "LNP", "Lag", "LagTot"):
307:         F.append(Finding("total_not_named_ltotal", "warn", f"the single root is `{roots[0]}`, not LTotal", None))
308:     field_tokens = set(class_names) | {c + "bar" for c in class_names} | SM_FIELDS_ALL
309:     for c in classes:
310:         for m in re.finditer(r"ClassMembers\s*->\s*\{([^}]*)\}", c["body"]):
311:             field_tokens |= {x.strip() for x in m.group(1).split(",") if x.strip()}
312:     for t in terms:

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Deterministic lints for an agent-written FeynRules add-on (.fr) file.

Every rule encodes one construct that broke a compile, a FeynRules check or a
MadGraph import in the benchmark (prompt_addendum_v3.txt rules 9-15 and the
repair-loop taxonomy). A lint runs in milliseconds on the text; the compile it
predicts takes up to 900 s.

Each finding carries the STAGE it predicts:
  compile  - FeynRules will not load or will not finish the model
  checks   - the model loads but a consistency check fails
  mg5      - the UFO is written but MadGraph rejects it
  harness  - the validation harness cannot pick the total Lagrangian
  warn     - FeynRules warns; the run may still pass

Library: ``lint_text(text) -> list[Finding]``. CLI: ``fr_lint.py file.fr``.

## Objective
- Extract the complete new-physics content of the HeavyN model (arXiv:1602.06957) into `spec.json` (a `FeynRulesModel` JSON, `model_name` = "HeavyN_gen") in the working directory, then run `./frgen spec.json` and iterate; final message must be the self-audit table.
- Work only inside `/private/var/folders/pf/fm0v0g_52r754cfv3r4lqv980000gn/T/ob-HeavyN-md9v1jbj/`.

## Important Details
- Bash is DENIED except `./frgen *` and `./frgen`; use read/glob/write tools only. Full `TASK.md` read was truncated in context — its numbered rules (1–15) are referenced by the agent's reasoning and partially restated below.
- Schema rules taken from TASK.md: all numeric physics values are STRINGS (`"-1/3"`, `"1500."`); SM add-on => `gauge_groups []`; built-in indices (Colour/Gluon/Generation/SU2D/SU2W) need no `index_decls`; any other index needs an `index_decls` entry (range_kind "NoUnfold", correct size); every particle needs a unique `class_index`; `self_conjugate=false` for complex fields, true for real/Majorana.
- Rule 1: write a named kinetic + mass term for every new class using the mass symbol from `Mass -> {M, value}`, added to the total Lagrangian; Majorana free term = `I/2 psibar.Ga[mu].del[psi, mu] - 1/2 M psibar.psi`.
- Rule 2: new couplings External unless clearly derived; use the paper's benchmark values for dimensionless couplings.
- Rule 3: charge-conjugate fermions (`psi^c`, `\bar{psi^c}`, Majorana mass eigenstates in chiral currents) must be written as `CC[psi]` / `bar[CC[psi]]`, never the bare field.
- Rule 4: SM Yukawas idiom: `QLbar.dR Phi[ii]`, `LLbar.lR Phi[ii]`, `QLbar.uR Phibar[jj] Eps[ii, jj]`; same-conjugation-type objects contract with `Eps[ii, jj]`.
- Rule 5: new U(1) charges only if the paper has a new gauge group (HeavyN does not).
- Rule 7: `paper/1602.06957_source.tex` LaTeX is authoritative.
- Rule 8: mass-eigenstate diagonalisation (incl. nu-N mixing) -> declare mixing angle External/Internal and express gauge eigenstates in `Definitions` of Unphysical classes; mixing in `Definitions` only allowed when 2+ referenced fields are declared.
- Rule 9: declared-before-used ordering (ordering is `kind:sequence` = `parameter`, `index_decl`, `particle_class`, `lagrangian_term`).
- Rule 12: no pattern rules (`X[i_, j_] :> ...`, `_?NumericQ` banned); `Definitions -> {X -> value}` allowed.
- Rule 13: matrix form for flavour couplings (`uqbar.VCKMR.Ga[mu].ProjP.dq`, `LLbar.yN.NR`) NOT explicit index sums `VCKMR[ff1, ff2] uqbar[...]`; banned constructs: `Index[Generation, ...]`, nested `Index[Generation, Index[Generation...]]`, explicit generation-index sums, `_?NumericQ`, pattern-rules, bare `del` on complex scalars, projectors on different chiralities in one term, `FeynmanGauge=True`, new particle with no class.
- Rule 14: every new class referenced in ≥1 term; fieldless terms rejected.
- Rule 15: every parameter used in a term declared with a numeric default; Majorana mass term must be `-1/2 M psibar.psi`.
- `fr_lint.py` keys: `FR_SYMBOLS`, `PROTECTED` (no naming collisions), `_reserved_mass_width_names` (parameters named in a class `Mass`/`Width` spec are dropped from `M$Parameters` unless they are Internal/have Definitions — re-declaring them causes duplicate UFO definitions), `DiagonalMatrix`/`Transpose`/`Inverse` are in the lint's declared-builtin list, `missing_interaction_order` check skips terms whose name matches `kin|Kin|KIN|free|Free|Gauge|gauge` and terms whose used params include one carrying an `InteractionOrder` or an SM coupling from `{ee,gw,gs,g1,yl,yu,yd,lam,CKM}`; `mass -> {sym}` extraction grabs the FIRST symbol for the Majorana-half check (pattern `MN ... NRbar . NR` within 40 chars).
- `fr_lint.py` `SM_FR` points to `~/Documents/Github/heptapod/...` (nonexistent) so SM-name-collision lints are inert, but still avoid SM names.
- Physics content decided so far (from paper reading):
  - New particle: heavy Majorana neutrino N — fermion, colour singlet, SU(2) singlet, Q=0, Y=0, LeptonNumber not assigned (SelfConjugate->True forces no QuantumNumbers; L violated by construction).
  - Plan: class `NR` with `ClassMembers {n1, n2, n3}`, `FlavorIndex Generation` (paper's MadGraph commands use `n2`, implying n1/n2/n3 exist; completeness scoring favours all mass eigenstates); unique class_index.
  - Mass spec form mirroring SM.fr: `Mass -> {MN, {mN1, 500.}, {mN2, 500.}, {mN3, 500.}}` (500. = paper's benchmark m_N; all degenerate, justified by paper treating a single eigenstate mass m_N).
  - Do NOT declare `MN`/`mN1..3` in `M$Parameters` (FR auto-declares from Mass spec; duplicating breaks UFO).
  - New parameter `VN` (paper's V_{lN}): tensor indices `{Generation, Generation}`, External, dimensionless, unique BlockName (e.g. `NMIXING`, no OrderBlock for tensors), `InteractionOrder {NP,1}`, 9 explicit `value_rules`. Index convention chosen as VN[heavy, light] = V*_{lN} so matrix products read `bar[CC[NR]].VN...` without Transpose. Diagonal default value: leaning `1.` (paper's bare cross-section sigma_0 definition sets |V_Nl| = 1) vs `0.01` (upper end of the paper's 10^-3–10^-2 range) — still unresolved, must be justified in Description.
  - `M$InteractionOrderHierarchy` must include `{NP,1}` (e.g. `{{QCD,1},{QED,2},{NP,1}}`).
  - Chirality projectors: FeynRules `ProjM` = P_L = (1-gamma5)/2, `ProjP` = P_R (confirmed from SM.fr `LL[sp1_,1,ff_] :> ProjM[sp1,sp2] vl[sp2,ff]`). So paper's `gamma^mu P_L` -> `.Ga[mu].ProjM`.
  - Planned terms (each wrapped in `ExpandIndices[..., FlavorExpand -> {...}]` as needed, since fields/params are written index-free):
    - `LNkin`: `I/2 NRbar.Ga[mu].del[NR, mu] - 1/2 NRbar.DiagonalMatrix[{mN1, mN2, mN3}].NR` (mass symbol from Mass spec used via member symbols).
    - `LWN`: `-gw/Sqrt[2] W[mu] bar[CC[NR]].VN.Ga[mu].ProjM.l + HC[...]`
    - `LZN`: `-gw/(2 cw) Z[mu] bar[CC[NR]].VN.Ga[mu].ProjM.vl + HC[...]` (Z term is not Hermitian alone -> needs HC).
    - `LHN`: `-gw mN/(2 MW) h bar[CC[NR]].VN.ProjM.vl + HC[...]` — mass factor per-generation unresolved (matrix vs scalar `MN`).
    - `LTotal` = sum of the above.
  - Charges verified for audit: W(+1)+N(0)+l(-1)=0; Z,N,nu all 0; h,N,nu 0.
  - Light neutrinos/leptons reuse SM fields `vl`, `l`, `LL` (SM.fr: `LL` Y=-1/2, `lR` Y=-1, `vl`/`l` carry only LeptonNumber/Q).
  - Diagonal Z coupling `Nbar^c gamma^mu N^c` vanishes identically for Majorana fields (why the paper omits it) — confirms Majorana N.

## Work State
### Completed
- Read `TASK.md` (partially truncated), `tools/frgen/frmodel.py`, `tools/fr_lint.py`, `tools/frgen/render.py`, `tools/frgen/templates/model.fr.j2`, `frgen` wrapper, `SM.fr`, and `paper/1602.06957_source.tex` (read was truncated; HeavyN Lagrangian lines 195–228 recovered in context).
- Directory inventory via `glob` (bash `ls` denied): `TASK.md`, `SM.fr`, `frgen`, `tools/fr_lint.py`, `tools/frgen/{__init__.py,render.py,frmodel.py,templates/model.fr.j2}`, `paper/1602.06957_source.tex`.
- Established field/projector conventions from `SM.fr`, lint rules, and renderer reserved-name behaviour.
- Model design largely decided (particles, class_members, mass spec, parameter `VN`, term list, matrix-form idioms).

### Active
- Deciding whether/how to include the Feynman-gauge Goldstone (`GP`, `G0`) couplings the paper says it added ("We implement the above Lagrangian with Goldstone boson couplings in the Feynman gauge"): deriving them from a Higgs-doublet operator yields an unwanted off-diagonal nu-N vev mass term (mass basis should be diagonal); a by-hand `h -> i G0` / charged `GP` substitution (coefficient `g m_N/(2 M_W)` = `m_N/vev`) is the alternative.
- Resolving the h-term mass factor for the 3-member class (scalar `MN` vs `DiagonalMatrix[{mN1,mN2,mN3}]`) and the final default value of `VN` (`1.` vs `0.01`).

### Blocked
- Full text of `TASK.md` beyond the truncation point (self-audit table format and TOOLKIT iteration instructions) not in context — must re-read the tail of `TASK.md` before finishing.

## Next Move
1. Re-read `TASK.md` from where it was truncated to recover the TOOLKIT instructions and exact self-audit table format.
2. Decide the Goldstone-coupling question and the `VN` default, then write `spec.json` (order: parameter `VN`, `particle_class` NR, `lagrangian_term`s LNkin/LWN/LZN/LHN/LTotal) and run `./frgen spec.json`, iterating on renderer/lint output.

## Relevant Files
- `TASK.md`: authoritative instructions (must be re-read to the end).
- `paper/1602.06957_source.tex`: authoritative paper source (LaTeX Lagrangian around lines 195–228).
- `tools/frgen/frmodel.py`: pydantic `FeynRulesModel` schema the spec must satisfy.
- `tools/frgen/render.py`: renders spec.json to `.fr`; reserved mass/width name dropping, `_is_internal_param`, block-entry collision rules.
- `tools/fr_lint.py`: deterministic lint rules the generated `.fr` is judged against.
- `SM.fr`: SM field/parameter/index conventions to build the add-on against (`gauge_groups []`).
- `frgen`: wrapper script; only permitted bash command (`./frgen spec.json`).
- `spec.json`: output to be written in the current directory (not yet created).
Continue if you have next steps, or stop and ask for clarification if you are unsure how to proceed.

1. Free-field terms for every new particle class. Write a named kinetic + mass term for each new field even when the paper shows only L_int. Use the mass symbol declared in the class `Mass -> {M, value}`. Add the term to the total Lagrangian sum.

2. Explicit EFT cutoffs. When the paper writes an operator with `1/Lambda^n` (or `1/M^n`, `1/f^n`), declare each distinct cutoff as an External parameter in GeV with the paper's benchmark value, e.g. `Lam == { ParameterType -> External, Value -> 1000., BlockName -> CUTOFF, InteractionOrder -> {QED, -1}, Description -> "EFT cutoff [GeV], Eq.(N)" }`. When the paper writes a fermion with a charge-conjugation superscript (`psi^c`, `\bar{psi^c}`, `psi^T C`, or a Majorana mass eigenstate that enters a chiral current with the opposite chirality), write it as `CC[psi]` (and `bar[CC[psi]]` for the conjugated bar). Never write the bare field. If the paper's benchmark sets that term's coefficient to zero, either drop the term or write it with `CC[...]`; never keep the term with the conjugation dropped. 4. SU(2) doublet contractions. Use the SM.fr conventions the add-on loads on: `Phi` has Y = +1/2, `LL` has Y = -1/2, `QL` has Y = +1/6, `Phi[1] = -I GP`, `Phi[2] = (vev + H + I G0)/Sqrt[2]`. Contract two objects of the same conjugation type (`LLbar` with `Phibar`, `QLbar` with `Phibar`, i.e. any term the paper writes with `Htilde = i tau2 H*`) with `Eps[ii, jj]` on two distinct indices: `LLbar[sp, ii, ff] ... Report which sign you chose and why. Do not put quantum numbers on a `SelfConjugate -> True` class; put a chiral charge on an Unphysical chiral class instead.

6. Read only the paper. Do not open any cached or reference `.fr` file for the same model. If you see one, say so in the output and do not use it.

7. Fractions and roots in extracted equations. The paper text is machine-extracted. A displayed fraction or radical can arrive flattened: the numerator, the fraction bar and the denominator become separate lines, so `A / Sqrt[B]` and `A Sqrt[B]` look identical. For every coefficient that contains a fraction, a square root or a power:

384: def _references(text: str, name: str) -> bool:
385:     """True if ``name`` appears in ``text`` as a whole Mathematica token."""
386:     if not text:
387:         return False
388:     return re.search(rf"(?<![A-Za-z0-9$]){re.escape(name)}(?![A-Za-z0-9$])", text) is not None

391: def _param_refs(p: Parameter, names: set) -> set:
392:     """Names of other parameters referenced by ``p``'s value/rules/definitions."""
393:     texts: List[str] = []
394:     if p.value:
395:         texts.append(p.value)
396:     for r in p.value_rules:
397:         texts.append(r.rhs)
398:     for r in p.definitions:
399:         texts.append(r.rhs)
400:     blob = " ".join(texts)
401:     return {n for n in names if n != p.name and _references(blob, n)}

404: def topo_sort_parameters(params: List[Parameter]) -> List[Parameter]:
405:     """Order parameters so each is defined before others that reference it.
406: 
407:     Stable (preserves input order among independent params). Raises on a
408:     dependency cycle.
409:     """
410:     names = {p.name for p in params}
411:     deps = {p.name: _param_refs(p, names) for p in params}
412:     by_name = {p.name: p for p in params}
413: 
414:     ordered: List[Parameter] = []
415:     emitted: set = set()
416:     remaining = [p.name for p in params]  # preserve input order
417: 
418:     while remaining:
419:         progressed = False
420:         still: List[str] = []
421:         for n in remaining:
422:             if deps[n] <= emitted:
423:                 ordered.append(by_name[n])
424:                 emitted.add(n)
425:                 progressed = True
426:             else:
427:                 still.append(n)
428:         remaining = still
429:         if not progressed:
430:             raise ValueError(
431:                 f"cyclic parameter dependency among: {sorted(remaining)}"
432:             )
433:     return ordered
434: 
435: 
436: _INDEX_SIZE = {"Generation": 3, "Colour": 3, "Gluon": 8, "SU2D": 2, "SU2W": 3}
437: 
438: 
439: def _block_entries(p: Parameter, sizes: Dict[str, int]) -> set:
440:     """The LHA entries (index tuples) an External parameter occupies in its block."""
441:     if not p.is_tensor:
442:         return {(p.order_block,)} if p.order_block is not None else set()
443:     entries = set()
444:     for r in p.value_rules:
445:         m = re.fullmatch(rf"\s*{re.escape(p.name)}\s*\[([0-9,\s]+)\]\s*", r.lhs)
446:         if m:
447:             entries.add(tuple(int(x) for x in m.group(1).split(",")))
448:     if entries:
449:         return entries
450:     ranges = [range(1, sizes.get(i, 3) + 1) for i in p.indices]
451:     out = {()}
452:     for rg in ranges:
453:         out = {e + (k,) for e in out for k in rg}
454:     return out

457: def _check_block_collisions(params: List[Parameter], sizes: Dict[str, int]) -> None:
458:     """External parameters that share an LHA block must not share an entry.
459: 
460:     FeynRules files an External tensor's entries under (block, i, j) and a
461:     scalar under (block, OrderBlock). Two parameters on one entry leave the UFO
462:     with one name defined twice, and MadGraph rejects the model ("name VLq1x1
463:     define multiple time"). Tensors of different rank in one block do not
464:     collide: GeneralU1's yN[i] and ynu[i,j] share a block and import cleanly.
465:     """
466:     by_block: Dict[str, List[Parameter]] = {}
467:     for p in params:
468:         if p.parameter_type == ParamType.External and p.block_name:
469:             by_block.setdefault(p.block_name, []).append(p)
470:     for block, ps in by_block.items():
471:         owner: Dict[tuple, str] = {}
472:         for p in ps:
473:             for e in sorted(_block_entries(p, sizes)):
474:                 if e in owner and owner[e] != p.name:
475:                     raise ValueError(
476:                         f"External parameters {owner[e]} and {p.name} both occupy "
477:                         f"block {block!r} entry {list(e)}: the UFO would define one "
478:                         "name twice. Give one of them its own block_name (or, for "
479:                         "scalars, its own order_block)"
480:                     )
481:                 owner[e] = p.name

510:

64: Motivated by TeV-scale neutrino mass models, we propose a systematic treatment of heavy neutrino $(N)$ production at hadron colliders.
65: 
66: Our simple and efficient modeling of the vector boson fusion (VBF) $W^\pm\gamma\rightarrow N\ell^\pm$ and $N\ell^\pm+nj$ signal definitions
67: resolve collinear and soft divergences that have plagued past studies, and is applicable to other color-singlet processes, 
68: e.g., associated Higgs $(W^\pm h)$,  sparticle $(\tilde{\ell}^\pm\tilde{\nu_\ell})$, and charged Higgs $(h^{\pm\pm}h^{\mp})$ production.
69: 
70: We present, for the first time, a comparison of all leading $N$ production modes, 
71: including both gluon fusion (GF) $gg\rightarrow Z^*/h^*\rightarrow N\overset{(-)}{\nu_\ell}$ and VBF.
72: 
73: We obtain fully differential results up to next-to-leading order (NLO) in QCD accuracy 
74: using a Monte Carlo tool chain linking FeynRules, N{\small LO}CT, and MadGraph5\_aMC@NLO.
75: Associated model files are publicly available.
76: At the 14 TeV LHC, the leading order GF rate is small and comparable to the NLO $N\ell^\pm+1j$ rate;
77: at a future 100 TeV Very Large Hadron Collider, GF dominates for $m_N={300-1500}$ GeV, beyond which VBF takes lead.

87: \section{Introduction}\label{sec:Intro}
88: 
89: The origin of neutrino masses $m_\nu$ that are tiny compared to all other fermion masses is a broad issue
90: in particle physics, cosmology, and astrophysics.
91: Nonzero $m_\nu$ imply the existence of new particles~\cite{Ma:1998dn},
92: but more generally, physics beyond the Standard Model (BSM) that may be observable at current and future experiments.
93: Extended neutrino mass 
94: models~\cite{Pilaftsis:1991ug,Kersten:2007vk,Gu:2008yj,Dev:2009aw,Zhang:2009ac,Adhikari:2010yt,Chen:2013fna,Dev:2013oxa,Dev:2015vra} based on the
95: Type I~\cite{Minkowski:1977sc,Yanagida:1979as,VanNieuwenhuizen:1979hm,Ramond:1979py,Glashow:1979nm,Mohapatra:1979ia,
96: GellMann:1980vs,Schechter:1980gr,Shrock:1980ct,Schechter:1981cv}, 
97: Inverse~\cite{Mohapatra:1986aw,Mohapatra:1986bd,Bernabeu:1987gr}, and 
98: Linear Seesaw Mechanisms~\cite{Akhmedov:1995ip,Akhmedov:1995vm}, 
99: feature heavy mass eigenstates $N_{i}$ that couple to electroweak (EW) bosons via mixing with left-handed (LH) neutrinos $\nu_{L}$.
100: In these TeV-scale scenarios, active-sterile mixing can be as large as  $\vert V_{\ell N_i}\vert\sim10^{-3}-10^{-2}$, 
101: and consistent with oscillation and EW data~\cite{Atre:2009rg,Antusch:2014woa,deGouvea:2015euy},
102: as well as direct searches by the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) experiments~\cite{Aaij:2014aba,Aad:2015xaa,Khachatryan:2016olu}.
103: Thus, if kinematically accessible, 
104: hadron colliders can produce heavy neutrinos that
105: decay to lepton number- and/or flavor-violating final states with observable rates.
106: 
107: 
108: 
109: For heavy $N$ masses $m_N$ above the EW scale, a systematic comparison of all leading single $N$ production modes cataloged 
110: in~\cite{Keung:1983uu,Datta:1993nm} has never been performed.
111: Most investigations focus on the charge current (CC) Drell-Yan (DY) 
112: process~\cite{Keung:1983uu,Pilaftsis:1991ug,Han:2006ip,delAguila:2006bda,delAguila:2007qnc,Atre:2009rg},
113: as shown in Fig.~\ref{fig:diagrams}(a),
114: \begin{equation}
115:  q ~\overline{q'} \rightarrow W^* \rightarrow N ~\ell^\pm, ~\quad q \in \{u,c,d,s,b\},
116:  \label{eq:DYCC}
117: \end{equation}
118: and has recently been found to be subleading in parts of this mass regime~\cite{Hessler:2014ssa,Alva:2014gxa}.
119: Missing in most analyses is the gluon fusion (GF) channel~\cite{Hessler:2014ssa},
120: which proceeds at leading order (LO) through quark triangles in Fig.~\ref{fig:diagrams}(b),
121: \begin{equation}
122:  g ~g \rightarrow h^*/Z^* \rightarrow N ~ \overset{(-)}{\nu_\ell}.
123:  \label{eq:GF}
124: \end{equation}
125: Variants of Eq.~(\ref{eq:GF}) have been studied elsewhere~\cite{BhupalDev:2012zg,Batell:2015aha}.
126: Formally, GF is a finite next-to-next-to-leading order in QCD correction to the neutral current (NC) DY process
127: \begin{eqnarray}
128:  q ~\overline{q} \rightarrow Z^* \rightarrow N ~\overset{(-)}{\nu_\ell}.
129:  \label{eq:DYNC}
130: \end{eqnarray}
131: 
132: Recent analyses have investigated the sizable EW vector boson fusion (VBF) 
133: process~\cite{Dev:2013wba,Bambhaniya:2014hla,Alva:2014gxa,Deppisch:2015qwa,Ng:2015hba,Arganda:2015ija,Das:2015toa}:
134: \begin{equation}
135:  q_{1} ~q_{2} ~\overset{W\gamma+WZ~\text{Fusion}}{\longrightarrow} ~N ~\ell^\pm ~q_{1}' ~q_{2}',
136:  \label{eq:VBF}
137: \end{equation}
138: and subleading CC DY with $n\geq1$ QCD jets~\cite{Dev:2013wba,Das:2014jxa,Das:2015toa}:
139: \begin{equation}
140:  p ~p \rightarrow W^{*}+ nj \rightarrow N\ell^\pm+  nj, \quad p,j\in\{\overset{(-)}{q},g\},
141:  \label{eq:DYnj}
142: \end{equation}
143: but with conflicting results.
144: The last two processes are plagued by soft and collinear poles in $s$- and $t$-channel exchanges of massless gauge bosons, 
145: issues usually associated with perturbative QCD, and require care~\cite{Alva:2014gxa,Ruiz:2015zca}.
146: E.g., inadequately regulated diverges are responsible for the overestimated 
147: cross sections claimed in~\cite{Dev:2013wba,Das:2014jxa,Deppisch:2015qwa,Das:2015toa}
148: 
149: 
150: We introduce a treatment that resolves all these issues.
151: Our results have widespread implications for SM and BSM physics:
152: the prescriptions for Eqs.~(\ref{eq:VBF}) and (\ref{eq:DYnj}) are applicable to, among other processes,
153: associated Higgs $(W^\pm h)$,  sparticle $(\tilde{\ell}^\pm\tilde{\nu_\ell})$, and charged Higgs $(h^{\pm\pm}h^{\mp})$ production.
154: 
155: To date, our study is the most accurate and comprehensive presentation of heavy $N$ production mechanisms at colliders.
156: It represents the first time properties of infrared and collinear (IRC) safety have been so rigorously imposed in this context, particularly to VBF.
157: 
158: Furthermore, we obtain modest next-to-leading order (NLO) in QCD corrections, demonstrating the stability of our approach.
