197: \section{Heavy Neutrino Model}\label{sec:Theory}
198: 
199: For  
200: $i~(m) =1,\dots,3$, LH (light) states and 
201: $j~(m')=1,\dots,n$, right-handed (heavy) states,
202: chiral neutrinos can be expanded into mass eigenstates by the rotation
203: \begin{eqnarray}
204: \begin{pmatrix} \nu_{Li} \\  N_{Rj}^c \end{pmatrix}
205: =
206: \begin{pmatrix} 
207: U_{3\times3} && V_{3\times n} \\
208: X_{n\times3} && Y_{n\times n}
209: \end{pmatrix}
210: \begin{pmatrix} \nu_{m} \\ N_{m'}^c \end{pmatrix}.
211: \end{eqnarray}
212: After rotating the charged leptons into the mass basis, 
213: which we take to be the identity matrix for simplicity,
214: $U_{3 \times3}$ is the observed light neutrino mixing matrix and
215: $V_{3 \times n}$ parameterizes active-heavy mixing. 
216: In the notation of~\cite{Atre:2009rg}, the flavor state $\nu_{\ell}$ in the mass basis is
217: \begin{equation}
218:  \nu_{\ell} = \sum_{m=1}^{3} U_{\ell m}\nu_{m} + \sum_{m'=1}^{n}V_{\ell m'} N^{c}_{m'}.
219: \end{equation}
220: For simplicity, we consider only one heavy mass eigenstate, labeled by $N$. This does not affect our conclusions.
221: The interaction Lagrangian with EW bosons is then
222: \begin{eqnarray}
223:   \mathcal{L}_{\rm Int.} = 
224:   &-& \frac{g}{\sqrt{2}}W^+_\mu		\sum_{\ell=e}^\tau \sum_{m=1}^3 ~\overline{\nu_m} ~U_{\ell m}^*	~\gamma^\mu P_L\ell^-\nonumber\\
225:   &-& \frac{g}{\sqrt{2}}W^+_\mu		\sum_{\ell=e}^\tau 		~\overline{N^c} ~V_{\ell N}^* 	~\gamma^\mu P_L\ell^-\nonumber\\
226:   &-& \frac{g}{2\cos\theta_W}Z_\mu	\sum_{\ell=e}^\tau \sum_{m=1}^3	~\overline{\nu_m} ~U_{\ell m}^*	~\gamma^\mu P_L\nu_\ell\nonumber\\
227:   &-& \frac{g}{2\cos\theta_W}Z_\mu	\sum_{\ell=e}^\tau 		~\overline{N^c} ~V_{\ell N}^*	~\gamma^\mu P_L\nu_\ell\nonumber\\
228:   &-& \frac{g m_N}{2M_W} h	\sum_{\ell=e}^\tau 		~\overline{N^c} ~V_{\ell N}^*	 P_L\nu_\ell + \text{H.c.}
229:   \label{eq:Lagrangian}
230: \end{eqnarray}
231: 
232: 
233: Precise values of $V_{\ell N}$ are model-dependent and are constrained by oscillation and collider experiments, 
234: tests of lepton universality, and $0\nu\beta\beta$-decay~\cite{Atre:2009rg,Antusch:2014woa,deGouvea:2015euy}.
235: However, $V_{\ell N}$ factorize in $N$ production cross sections such that
236: \begin{equation}
237:  \sigma(pp\rightarrow N~X) = \vert V_{N\ell}\vert^2 ~\times~ \sigma_{0}(pp\rightarrow N~X),
238: \end{equation}
239: where $\sigma_{0}$ is a model-independent ``bare'' cross section in which one sets $\vert V_{N\ell}\vert=1$.
240: Hence, our results are applicable to various heavy neutrino models.

244: \section{Computational Setup}\label{sec:MC}
245: 
246: We implement the above Lagrangian with Goldstone boson couplings in the Feynman gauge into FeynRules (FR) 2.3.10~\cite{Alloul:2013bka,Christensen:2008py}.
247: QCD renormalization and $R_2$ rational counterterms are calculated with \nloct~1.02 (prepackaged in FR)~\cite{Degrande:2014vpa} 
248: and FeynArts 3.8~\cite{Hahn:2000kx}.
249: Feynman rules are collected into a universal output file (UFO)~\cite{Degrande:2011ua} and is available publicly~\cite{nloFRModel}.
250: We obtain fully differential results using MadGraph5$\_$aMC$@$NLO  2.3.3~\cite{Alwall:2014hca}.
251: SM inputs are taken from the 2014 Particle Data Group~\cite{Agashe:2014kda}:
252: \begin{eqnarray}
253:  \alpha^{\rm \overline{MS}}(M_{Z})		&=& 1/127.940, \quad M_{Z}=91.1876\GeV, \nonumber\\ 
254:  \sin^{2}_{\rm \overline{MS}}(\theta_{W}) 	&=& 0.23126.
255:  \label{eq:smInputs}
256: \end{eqnarray}
257: We assume five massless quarks, take the Cabbibo-Kobayashi-Masakawa (CKM) matrix to be diagonal with unit entries,
258: and use the NLO NNPDF2.3 QED PDF (\texttt{lhaid:244600}) ~\cite{Ball:2013hta},
259: which features a $\gamma$-PDF with both elastic and inelastic components,
260: at collider energies of $\sqrt{s}=14$ and $100$ TeV. 
261: We extract $\alpha_s(\mu_r^2)$ from the PDFs.

266: \section{Infrared- and Collinear-Safe Hadron Collider Signal Definitions}\label{sec:SigDef}
267: 
268: To consistently compare channels and colliders, 
269: we follow the 2013 Snowmass recommendations~\cite{Avetisyan:2013onh}
270: and evaluate cross sections assuming the same fiducial acceptance.
271: In practice, however, one tunes cuts to specific colliders and final states.
272: Jet and charged lepton pseudorapidities $(\eta^{j,\ell})$ and charged lepton $p_T$ are required to satisfy~\cite{Avetisyan:2013onh}:
273: \begin{equation}
274:  \vert\eta^{j,\ell}\vert < 2.5, \quad p_T^\ell > 20\GeV.
275:  \label{eq:LepCuts}
276: \end{equation}
277: QCD radiation in Eq.~(\ref{eq:DYnj}) gives rise to fixed order (FO) cross sections that scale as powers of $\log(Q^2/q_T^2)$:
278: \begin{equation}
279:  \sigma(pp\rightarrow N\ell^\pm+nj) \sim \sum^n_k \alpha_s^k(Q^2)\log^{(2k-1)}\left(\frac{Q^2}{q_T^2}\right).
280:  \label{eq:qcdPowerSeries}
281: \end{equation}
282: $Q\sim m_N$ is the scale of the hard scattering process
283: and $q_T \equiv \sum_k^n p_{T,k}^{j}$ is the $(N\ell)$-system's transverse momentum,
284: which equals the sum of all jet $p_T$.
285: 
286: The perturbativity of these logarithms for TeV-scale leptons was studied in~\cite{Ruiz:2015zca}.
287: In the CSS $p_T$-resummation formalism~\cite{Collins:1984kg}, FO results are trustworthy when
288: $\alpha_s(Q^2)$ is perturbative, with $\Lambda_{\rm QCD} = 0.2\GeV$, and $q_T$ is comparable to $Q$:
289: \begin{equation}
290:  \log\frac{Q}{\Lambda_{\rm QCD}}\gg1 \quad\text{and}\quad \log^2\frac{Q}{q_T}\lesssim\log\frac{Q}{\Lambda_{\rm QCD}}.
291: \end{equation}
292: 
293: Imposing $Q = m_N$, jets in Eq.~(\ref{eq:qcdPowerSeries}) must satisfy
294: \begin{equation}
295:  \sum_k^n p_{T,k}^{j} \gtrsim m_N \times e^{-\sqrt{\log(m_N/\Lambda_{\rm QCD})}}.
296:  \label{eq:cssPTBound}
297: \end{equation}
298: Taking for example $n=1$ and $m_N$ up to $1~(1.5)\TeV$, the mass range of interest at 14 (100) TeV, this translates to
299: \begin{equation}
300:  p_T^j \gtrsim 55~(80)\GeV.
301: \end{equation}
302: Weaker $p_T^j$ cuts lead to artificially large logarithms and overestimated cross sections in Eq.~(\ref{eq:qcdPowerSeries}).
303: 
304: We cluster jets with FastJet~\cite{Cacciari:2005hq,Cacciari:2011ma} 
305: using the anti-$k_T$ algorithm~\cite{Cacciari:2008gp} with a separation parameter of $ \Delta R = 0.4$.
306: For differential events, we parton shower (PS) with Pythia 8.212~\cite{Sjostrand:2014zea}.
307: 
308: 
309: We equate the factorization and renormalization scales
310: to half the sum over final-state transverse masses (\texttt{dynamical\_scale\_choice=3} in \mgamc):
311: \begin{eqnarray}
312:  \mu_f, \mu_r, \mu_0 = \sum_{k=N,\ell,\text{jets}}\cfrac{m_{T,k}}{2} = \frac12\sum_{k} \sqrt{m_k^2 + p_{T,k}^2}.
313: \end{eqnarray}
314: 
315:

319: 
320: We quantify the scale dependence by varying it over
321: \begin{equation}
322:  0.5  \leq \mu/ \mu_0 \leq2.
323: \end{equation}

348: GF is a loop-induced process, which are only recently~\cite{Hirschi:2015iia} supported by \mgamc.

350: We therefore perform the LO calculation matched and merged with up to one additional jet via the MLM scheme \cite{Mangano:2006rw}.

375: The difficulty in modeling $W\gamma$ fusion stems from the $t$-channel photon propagator, 
376: which, like Eq.~(\ref{eq:qcdPowerSeries}) for $N\ell^\pm+nj$, gives rise to logarithms of the form~\cite{Alva:2014gxa}
377: \begin{equation}
378: d\sigma(q_{1}q_{2}\rightarrow N \ell^\pm q_{1}' q_{2}') \sim 
379: \log\left(\cfrac{m_N^2}{M_W^2}\right)\log\left(\cfrac{m_N^2}{p_T^{j_\gamma 2}}\right).
380: \label{eq:VBFLogs}
381: \end{equation}
382: Here, $p_T^{j_\gamma}$ is the $p_T$ of the jet associated with the photon exchange.
383: However, consistent treatment of Eq.~(\ref{eq:VBFLogs}) dictates $p_T^j$ cuts excessive for $\gamma$-initiated processes. 
384: A resolution is to collinearly factorize and resum the photon piece into a DGLAP-evolved $\gamma$-PDF, consider instead
385: \begin{equation}
386:  q ~\gamma \rightarrow N ~\ell^\pm ~q',
387:  \label{eq:qaScattering}
388: \end{equation}
389: and evolve the PDF to the hard scattering scale.
390: One loses the ability to efficiently tag a second forward/backward jet but gains a large (logarithmic) total rate enhancement~\cite{Alva:2014gxa}.
391: Eq.~(\ref{eq:qaScattering}) is realization of the structure function approach to VBF~\cite{Han:1992hr}.
392: Formally, the $N\ell^\pm qq'$ channel can be recovered by performing the ACOT-like jet matching explicitly as in~\cite{Alva:2014gxa}
393: or evaluating the NLO in QED corrections to Eq.~(\ref{eq:qaScattering}).
394: For VBF, we impose the $\eta^{j},p_T^{j}$ cuts of~\cite{Alva:2014gxa}:
395: \begin{equation}
396:  \vert\eta^{j_\VBF}\vert < 4.5, \quad p_T^{j_\VBF} > 30\GeV.
397: \end{equation}
398: Collinear poles associated with $t$-channel $\ell$ exchange emerge in Eq.~(\ref{eq:qaScattering}) but are regulated by cuts in Eq.~(\ref{eq:LepCuts}).
399: The process at NLO in QCD is simulated by

403: > add process a q > n2 mu q QED=3 QCD=0 [QCD]
404: > output PP_VBF_NLO; launch;
405: \end{verbatim}

511: \subsection{NLO+PS Kinematics at 14 TeV}
512: We now consider the differential distribution for the processes in Fig.~\ref{fig:diagrams} but focus largely on the VBF channel.
513: 
514: The kinematics of heavy lepton production from DY currents at NLO and NLO+Leading Log(recoil) was studied in~\cite{Ruiz:2015zca}.
515: There, the differential NLO $K$-factors, defined as
516: \begin{equation}
517:  K_{\mathcal{O}}^{\rm NLO} \equiv \cfrac{d\sigma^{\rm NLO}/d\mathcal{O}}{d\sigma^{\rm LO}/d\mathcal{O}}
518: \end{equation}
519: for observable $\mathcal{O}$, were analytically shown to be flat in the leading regions of phase space.
520: In these regions, NLO contributions are dominated by soft initial-state radiation, which generically factorize for DY processes.
521: We confirm the flatness of $K_{\mathcal{O}}^{\rm NLOPS}$ for the DY channels, 
522: including for complex observables such as cluster mass in the $N\ell\rightarrow 3\ell \nu$ final state.
523: 
524: 
525: The phenomenology of the GF channel has not been previously studied.
526: It is beyond the scope of this investigation to do so here and will be presented elsewhere.

528: 
529: At $\sqrt{s} = 14$ TeV and representative  neutrino mass $m_N = 500\GeV$,
530: the LO distributions for the $W\gamma$ fusion process was studied in Ref.~\cite{Alva:2014gxa}.

532: For the first time, we show in Fig.~\ref{fig:vbfDifferential} the NLO+PS (dash) and LO+PS (solid)-accurate distributions with respect to 
533: (a,c) $p_T$ and (b,d) rapidity $(y)$ of the (a,b) $N$- and (c,d) $(N\ell)$-systems. $K_{\mathcal{O}}^{\rm NLOPS}$ is shown in the lower panel.
534: 
535: For the two system, but particularly the $(N\ell)$-system, we observe a net migration at NLOPS of events from the lowest $p_T$ bins
536: resulting in $K^{\rm NLOPS}_{p_T}<1$ for these bins. At high $p_T$, $K^{\rm NLOPS}_{p_T}$ quickly converges to unity from above.
537: 
538: In the rapidity distributions, we observe a similar, but more pronounced, migration of events from large $y$ to smaller values,
539: consistent with shifts to larger $p_T$.
540: 
541: The charged lepton $p_T$ and $\eta$ distributions (not shown) demonstrate little sensitivity to $\mathcal{O}(\alpha_s)$ corrections.
542: However, as VBF is dominated by $\gamma\rightarrow \ell$ splittings~\cite{Alva:2014gxa}, 
543: one does not expect such sensitivity to QCD radiation until $\mathcal{O}(\alpha^2 \alpha_s)$.
544: 
545: Though numerically less significant, we find that the NLO corrections to the VBF distributions are qualitatively different than those of DY-like systems:
546: whereas differential $K$-factors for DY processes tend to remain flat and above unity,
547: QCD corrections for $W\gamma$ fusion tend to depopulate low-$p_T$/forward regions of phase space and populate high-$p_T$/central regions.
548: This results in $K$-factors both above and below unity.

568: \section{Summary and Conclusion}\label{sec:Conclusions}
569: 
570: The origin of light neutrino masses remains elusive.
571: Extended neutrino mass models predict the existence TeV-scale heavy neutrinos $N_i$ that may be discovered at current or future collider experiments.
572: 
573: We propose a systematic treatment of $N$ production mechanisms at hadron colliders, 
574: and provide instructions for building IRC-safe VBF and $N\ell^\pm+nj$ signal definitions.
575: The prescription remedies issues that have plagued past analyses,
576: and is applicable to a number of other SM and BSM processes.
577: We report modest NLO corrections, demonstrating the perturbative stability of our approach.
578: 
579: We present also the first NLOPS-accurate differential distributions for the $W\gamma$ VBF process.
580: We observe nontrivial differential $K$-factors below and above unity.
581: 
582: In a model-independent fashion,
583: we present for the first time a comparison of all leading single $N$ production modes at $\sqrt{s} = 14$ and $100$ TeV.
584: Fully differential results up to NLO in QCD accuracy are obtained through a MC tool chain linking FeynRules, \nloct, and \mgamc.
585: 
586: Associated model files are publicly available~\cite{nloFRModel}.

(***************************************************************************************************************)
(******                       This is the FeynRules mod-file for the Standard model                       ******)
(******                                                                                                   ******)
(******     Authors: N. Christensen, C. Duhr, B. Fuks                                                     ******)

(****** If set to False, unitary gauge is assumed.                                                          ****)
(****** Feynman gauge is especially useful for CalcHEP/CompHEP where the calculation is 10-100 times faster. ***)
(****** Feynman gauge is not supported in MadGraph and Sherpa.                                              ****)
(***************************************************************************************************************)

(* ************************** *)
(* *****  Information   ***** *)
(* ************************** *)
M$ModelName = "Standard Model";

M$Information = {
  Authors      -> {"N. Christensen", "C. Duhr", "B. Fuks"}, 
  Version      -> "1.4.7",
  Date         -> "28. 09. 2016",
  Institutions -> {"Michigan State University", "Universite catholique de Louvain (CP3)", "IPHC Strasbourg / University of Strasbourg"},
  Emails       -> {"neil@pa.msu.edu", "claude.duhr@uclouvain.be", "benjamin.fuks@cnrs.in2p3.fr"},
  URLs         -> "http://feynrules.phys.ucl.ac.be/view/Main/StandardModel"
};

FeynmanGauge = True;

(* ************************** *)
(* ***** NLO Variables ****** *)
(******************************)

FR$LoopSwitches = {{Gf, MW}};
FR$RmDblExt = { ymb -> MB, ymc -> MC, ymdo -> MD, yme -> Me, 
   ymm -> MMU, yms -> MS, ymt -> MT, ymtau -> MTA, ymup -> MU};

(* ************************** *)
(* *****  Change  log   ***** *)
(* ************************** *)

(* v1.4.7: Index issue with the ghost Lagrangian (special thanks to S. Iwamoto *)
(* v1.4.6: NLO variable added.                                               *)
(* v1.4.5: Added widths for ghosts.                                          *)
(* v1.4.4: Changed widths of goldstone bosons to be the same as for the W and Z bosons *)
(* v1.4.3: Updated conventions for the symmetric structure constants of SU3. *)
(* v1.4.2: Set FeynmanGauge=True as default again.                           *)
(* v1.4: Added SU(2) representation.                                         *)
(*       -> Modification in the field declarations (doublets are added)      *)
(*       -> Modification in the Lagrangian (much simpler).                   *)
(* v1.3: Added yukawa couplings for all fermions for gauge invariance.       *)
(*       Added yukawa couplings for 1st generation fermions to Massless.rst. *)
(*       Updated parameters to PDG 2010.                                     *)
(* v1.2: Set FeynmanGauge=True as default.                                   *)
(*       Set Gluonic ghosts to be included in both gauges.                   *)
(* v1.1: Fixed yukawa couplings in Feynman gauge.                            *)
(*       Changed yd[n] CKM[n,m] to yd[m] CKM[n,m].                           *)
(*       Changed yu[n] Conjugate[CKM[m,n]] to yu[m] Conjugate[CKM[m,n]].     *)

(* ************************** *)
(* *****      vevs      ***** *)
(* ************************** *)
M$vevs = { {Phi[2],vev} };

(* ************************** *)
(* *****  Gauge groups  ***** *)
(* ************************** *)
M$GaugeGroups = {
  U1Y  == { 
    Abelian          -> True,  
    CouplingConstant -> g1, 
    GaugeBoson       -> B, 
    Charge           -> Y
  },
  SU2L == { 
    Abelian           -> False, 
    CouplingConstant  -> gw, 
    GaugeBoson        -> Wi, 
    StructureConstant -> Eps, 
    Representations   -> {Ta,SU2D}, 
    Definitions       -> {Ta[a_,b_,c_]->PauliSigma[a,b,c]/2, FSU2L[i_,j_,k_]:> I Eps[i,j,k]}
  },
  SU3C == { 
    Abelian           -> False, 
    CouplingConstant  -> gs, 
    GaugeBoson        -> G,
    StructureConstant -> f, 
    Representations   -> {T,Colour}, 
    SymmetricTensor   -> dSUN
  } 
};


(* ************************** *)
(* *****    Indices     ***** *)
(* ************************** *)

IndexRange[Index[SU2W      ]] = Unfold[Range[3]]; 
IndexRange[Index[SU2D      ]] = Unfold[Range[2]];
IndexRange[Index[Gluon     ]] = NoUnfold[Range[8]];
IndexRange[Index[Colour    ]] = NoUnfold[Range[3]]; 
IndexRange[Index[Generation]] = Range[3];

IndexStyle[SU2D,       k];

IndexStyle[Generation, f];

(* *** Interaction orders *** *)
(* ***  (as used by mg5)  *** *)

  {QCD, 1},
  {QED, 2}
};

(* **** Particle classes **** *)

(* Gauge bosons: physical vector fields *)

    Mass            -> 0,  
    Width           -> 0,  
    ParticleName    -> "a", 
    PDG             -> 22,

## Objective

- Rule 1: named kinetic + mass term for every new class using the mass symbol from `Mass -> {M, value}`, added to `LTotal`; Majorana free term = `I/2 psibar.Ga[mu].del[psi, mu] - 1/2 M psibar.psi`.
- Rule 2: new couplings External unless clearly derived; use paper benchmark values for dimensionless couplings.
- Rule 3: charge-conjugate fermions (`psi^c`, `\bar{psi^c}`, Majorana mass eigenstates in chiral currents) → `CC[psi]` / `bar[CC[psi]]`, never the bare field. For Majorana N, `\overline{N^c}` = `bar[CC[NR]]`.
- Rule 4: SM Yukawa idioms `QLbar.dR Phi[ii]`, `LLbar.lR Phi[ii]`, `QLbar.uR Phibar[jj] Eps[ii, jj]`; same-conjugation objects contract with `Eps[ii, jj]`.
- Rule 5: no new gauge group (HeavyN has none) → no new U(1) charges.
- Rule 7: `paper/1602.06957_source.tex` LaTeX is authoritative.
- Rule 8: mass-eigenstate diagonalisation (incl. ν-N mixing) → declare mixing angle and express gauge eigenstates in `Definitions` of Unphysical classes; `Definitions` only when 2+ referenced fields declared.

NRbar . NR` within 40 chars using the FIRST symbol of `mass -> {sym}`.

  - `LWN`: `-gw/Sqrt[2] W[mu] bar[CC[NR]].VN.Ga[mu].ProjM.l + HC[...]`

AUTOMATIC CHECK: after every write or edit of spec.json the toolkit runs by itself and
its report is appended to that tool's result. Read it after each change and fix what it
reports. You may still run `./frgen spec.json` yourself.

## Physics-completeness rules (apply to every model)

1. Free-field terms for every new particle class. Write a named kinetic + mass term for each new field even when the paper shows only L_int. Use the mass symbol declared in the class `Mass -> {M, value}`. Add the term to the total Lagrangian sum.
   - Real vector (gauge singlet): `LXkin := -1/4 FS[X, mu, nu] FS[X, mu, nu] + 1/2 MX^2 X[mu] X[mu];` (the explicit form `-1/4 (del[X[nu], mu] - del[X[mu], nu])^2` is equivalent).
   - Complex vector: `-1/2 FS[Xbar, mu, nu] FS[X, mu, nu] + MX^2 Xbar[mu] X[mu]`.
   - Complex scalar: `DC[phibar, mu] DC[phi, mu] - Mphi^2 phibar phi`. Real scalar: `1/2 del[phi, mu] del[phi, mu] - 1/2 Mphi^2 phi^2`.
   - Dirac fermion: `I psibar.Ga[mu].DC[psi, mu] - Mpsi psibar.psi`. Majorana fermion (`SelfConjugate -> True`): `I/2 psibar.Ga[mu].del[psi, mu] - 1/2 Mpsi psibar.psi`.

2. Explicit EFT cutoffs. When the paper writes an operator with `1/Lambda^n` (or `1/M^n`, `1/f^n`), declare each distinct cutoff as an External parameter in GeV with the paper's benchmark value, e.g. `Lam == { ParameterType -> External, Value -> 1000., BlockName -> CUTOFF, InteractionOrder -> {QED, -1}, Description -> "EFT cutoff [GeV], Eq.(N)" }`. Write the factor `1/Lam^(d-4)` verbatim in the term, with `d` the operator mass dimension you computed in the self-audit. Keep the paper's dimensionless couplings (kappa, lambda, c_i) dimensionless with the paper's benchmark defaults. Do this for the term and for its `HC[...]` partner. Only if the paper's own implementation absorbs `kappa/Lambda^n` into one coefficient may you do the same; then the parameter Description must say "= kappa/Lambda^n, mass dimension -n, units GeV^-n" and the default must equal the paper's numeric `kappa/Lambda^n`. Never leave a dimensionful coefficient with an unexplained O(0.1) default.

3. Charge conjugation. When the paper writes a fermion with a charge-conjugation superscript (`psi^c`, `\bar{psi^c}`, `psi^T C`, or a Majorana mass eigenstate that enters a chiral current with the opposite chirality), write it as `CC[psi]` (and `bar[CC[psi]]` for the conjugated bar). Never write the bare field. If the paper's benchmark sets that term's coefficient to zero, either drop the term or write it with `CC[...]`; never keep the term with the conjugation dropped. Use the class field with its Generation index (for example the SM class `vl[ff]`), not a class member like `ve[nn]`, because FeynRules reads an index on a class member as a spin index.

4. SU(2) doublet contractions. Use the SM.fr conventions the add-on loads on: `Phi` has Y = +1/2, `LL` has Y = -1/2, `QL` has Y = +1/6, `Phi[1] = -I GP`, `Phi[2] = (vev + H + I G0)/Sqrt[2]`. Contract a doublet with an anti-doublet on a shared index: `LLbar[sp, ii, ff] ... Phi[ii]`. Contract two objects of the same conjugation type (`LLbar` with `Phibar`, `QLbar` with `Phibar`, i.e. any term the paper writes with `Htilde = i tau2 H*`) with `Eps[ii, jj]` on two distinct indices: `LLbar[sp, ii, ff] ... Phibar[jj] Eps[ii, jj]`. Never contract `LLbar[ii]` with `Phibar[ii]`. Model the SM Yukawas: `QLbar.dR Phi[ii]`, `LLbar.lR Phi[ii]`, `QLbar.uR Phibar[jj] Eps[ii, jj]`.

5. New U(1) charges. Do not copy a paper's charge table literally when the paper's Yukawa equation and its table use different hypercharge conventions (for example the paper effectively uses Y(H) = -1/2). Re-derive the new-U(1) charge of every SM field, including the Higgs, from the requirement that all SM Yukawas and all new Yukawas are invariant under SM.fr conventions. Report which sign you chose and why. Do not put quantum numbers on a `SelfConjugate -> True` class; put a chiral charge on an Unphysical chiral class instead.

6. Read only the paper. Do not open any cached or reference `.fr` file for the same model. If you see one, say so in the output and do not use it.

7. Fractions and roots in extracted equations. The paper text is machine-extracted. A displayed fraction or radical can arrive flattened: the numerator, the fraction bar and the denominator become separate lines, so `A / Sqrt[B]` and `A Sqrt[B]` look identical. For every coefficient that contains a fraction, a square root or a power:
   - If a LaTeX source file (`*_source.tex`) is available, read the `\frac{...}{...}` and `\sqrt{...}` there and take it literally. The LaTeX is authoritative over the flattened text.
   - Otherwise cross-check the placement against a second equation of the paper that depends on the same coefficient (a partial width, a cross section, a limit, or a small-parameter expansion) and name that equation in the self-audit. A coupling `g/Sqrt[1-x]` gives a width proportional to `1/(1-x)`; a coupling `g Sqrt[1-x]` gives a width proportional to `(1-x)`.
   - If neither resolves it, choose the form that reproduces a numerical value the paper states, and say so.
   Never silently pick one placement.

8. Mass mixing. When the paper diagonalises a mass mixing between a new state and an SM state (Z-Z', h-S, W-W_R, nu-N), write the mass eigenstates the paper uses: declare the mixing angle (External, or Internal with the paper's formula) and express the gauge eigenstates through it in `Definitions` of Unphysical classes. Do not leave the mixing in a comment.

## FeynRules and UFO construct rules (each one broke a compile or a MadGraph import in earlier runs)

9. Non-fundamental colour representations. If a field carries a colour index other than the triplet `Colour` or the adjoint `Gluon` (for example a sextet), declare the index range AND add the representation line FeynRules needs, before the field declarations: `AddGaugeRepresentation[SU3C -> {T6, Sextet}];` for a sextet (schema: put both lines in `raw_preamble`; also keep the `index_decls` entry). Write covariant derivatives on the whole field, `DC[Phi, mu]`, never with an explicit colour index inside `DC[...]`.

10. Names. Class names, parameter names and index names must not be Mathematica built-ins or FeynRules symbols: never `N`, `C`, `D`, `E`, `I`, `K`, `O`, `HC`, `CC`, `FS`, `DC`, `del`, `Eps`, `Ga`, `ProjP`, `ProjM`, and never a name SM.fr already declares (`H`, `Phi`, `Z`, `W`, `A`, `G`, `ee`, `gs`, `gw`, `sw`, `cw`, `vev`, `MZ`, `MW`, ...). No primes or punctuation in `ParticleName`/`AntiParticleName` (`W'` is not a valid UFO name; write `Wp`, `Wpbar`). Use class indices of 100 or more for new classes.

11. Interaction orders. Every new coupling parameter (Yukawa, portal, quartic, new gauge coupling, dimensionless EFT coefficient) carries an `InteractionOrder`: `{NP, 1}` for a new-physics coupling, `{QED, 1}` or `{QCD, 1}` only when it is literally that coupling. Declare `M$InteractionOrderHierarchy` with every order you use (for example `{{QCD, 1}, {QED, 2}, {NP, 1}}`). A coupling with no order makes MadGraph reject the UFO ("Some couplings have '1' order").

12. Tensor parameters. Give every indexed parameter explicit per-component values (`yN[1,1] -> 0.1, yN[1,2] -> 0, ...`; schema: `value_rules`). Never use a pattern rule such as `X[i_?NumericQ, j_?NumericQ] :> ...` in `Definitions`: FeynRules exports the pattern verbatim as a UFO parameter name and MadGraph fails with an unrelated "invalid syntax" error.

13. Flavour structure in matrix form. Write generation-space couplings as matrix products between class fields, `uqbar.VCKMR.Ga[mu].ProjP.dq`, `LLbar.yN.NR`, `ISbar.Ga[mu].ProjM.IS`, not as explicit index sums `VCKMR[ff1, ff2] uqbar[ff1, cc]...dq[ff2, cc]`, and never nest one generation index inside another. Explicit-index forms leak FeynRules internals (`ConvertSpinToString`, `MakeIdenticalFermions`) into the UFO.

14. One declared total. Define exactly one Lagrangian term named `LTotal` that sums every other term you define, and make sure every other term appears in that sum. Do not define two alternative totals. Do not emit a term that contains no field (a pure constant): FeynRules exports it as a vertex with no particles.

15. Declarations. Every field used in a term is declared; every parameter used in a term is declared with a numeric default; every `SelfConjugate -> True` class has no `QuantumNumbers`; a Majorana mass term is `-1/2 M psibar.psi`.

## Mandatory self-audit table (produce it BEFORE the model)

For every Lagrangian term you emit, output one row of this table. Then fix any row that fails before you write the model.

| term name | fields in the monomial | operator mass dimension d | coupling symbol | coupling mass dimension (must be 4 - d) | 1/Lambda power present (must be d - 4, or "n/a" if d <= 4) | Q sum | Y sum | SU(2) contraction (singlet? which Eps or shared index) | SU(3) contraction | sum of each new U(1) charge (one column per U(1), must be 0) | lepton/baryon number sum (if the paper assigns them) | CC[] used where paper writes psi^c (yes/no/n/a) | fraction/root placement checked against (equation, LaTeX line, or "n/a") | Hermitian partner (HC[] or self-conjugate) |

Rules for the table:
- Field mass dimensions: scalar 1, vector 1, fermion 3/2, `FS[...]` 2, `del`/`DC` 1.
- Every Q sum, Y sum, and new-U(1) sum must equal 0. Use the charges you declared in `QuantumNumbers` and the SM.fr charges for SM fields. If a sum is not 0, the term is wrong; fix the contraction or the charge before you continue.
- If d > 4, the row must show `1/Lambda^(d-4)` and an External cutoff parameter, or a Description that states the absorbed dimension and units.
- Add one row per new particle class that confirms its kinetic + mass term exists and is in the total Lagrangian sum.
- Add one row per non-fundamental colour representation that confirms the `AddGaugeRepresentation[...]` line is present.
- Add one line under the table that lists every `SelfConjugate -> True` class and confirms it carries no `QuantumNumbers`.
- Add one line that lists every class, parameter and index name you chose and confirms none is a Mathematica built-in, a FeynRules symbol, or an SM.fr name.
- Add one line that names the single total Lagrangian and lists the terms it sums.
- Add one line that states whether any reference or cached model file was read (must be "none").

404: def topo_sort_parameters(params: List[Parameter]) -> List[Parameter]:
405:     """Order parameters so each is defined before others that reference it.

411:     deps = {p.name: _param_refs(p, names) for p in params}
412:     by_name = {p.name: p for p in params}

414:     ordered: List[Parameter] = []

416:     remaining = [p.name for p in params]  # preserve input order
417: 
418:     while remaining:
419:         progressed = False
420:         still: List[str] = []
421:         for n in remaining:
422:             if deps[n] <= emitted:
423:                 ordered.append(by_name[n])
424:                 emitted.add(n)
425:                 progressed = True
426:             else:
427:                 still.append(n)
428:         remaining = still

432:             )

440:     """The LHA entries (index tuples) an External parameter occupies in its block."""

478:                         "name twice. Give one of them its own block_name (or, for "
479:                         "scalars, its own order_block)"

"""Deterministic lints for an agent-written FeynRules add-on (.fr) file.

Every rule encodes one construct that broke a compile, a FeynRules check or a
MadGraph import in the benchmark (prompt_addendum_v3.txt rules 9-15 and the
repair-loop taxonomy). A lint runs in milliseconds on the text; the compile it
predicts takes up to 900 s.

Each finding carries the STAGE it predicts:
  compile  - FeynRules will not load or will not finish the model
  checks   - the model loads but a consistency check fails
  mg5      - the UFO is written but MadGraph rejects it
  harness  - the validation harness cannot pick the total Lagrangian
  warn     - FeynRules warns; the run may still pass

Library: ``lint_text(text) -> list[Finding]``. CLI: ``fr_lint.py file.fr``.
"""

197: \section{Heavy Neutrino Model}\label{sec:Theory}
198: 
199: For

202: chiral neutrinos can be expanded into mass eigenstates by the rotation

204: \begin{pmatrix} \nu_{Li} \\  N_{Rj}^c \end{pmatrix}
205: =
206: \begin{pmatrix} 
207: U_{3\times3} && V_{3\times n} \\
208: X_{n\times3} && Y_{n\times n}
209: \end{pmatrix}
210: \begin{pmatrix} \nu_{m} \\ N_{m'}^c \end{pmatrix}.
211: \end{eqnarray}

214: $U_{3 \times3}$ is the observed light neutrino mixing matrix and
215: $V_{3 \times n}$ parameterizes active-heavy mixing.

229:   \label{eq:Lagrangian}

13: and CARRY the irregular parts (Lagrangian algebra, mixing blocks, NLO
14: bookkeeping) as verbatim Mathematica strings.

16: All numeric fields are strings so exact FeynRules syntax survives untouched:
17: rationals like ``-1/3``, decimals like ``1500.``, scientific ``2.5*^-3``.

28: # A verbatim numeric string: "-1/3", "1500.", "2.5*^-3", "Internal", "Automatic".
29: NumberStr = str
30: 
31: _OPEN = {"(": ")", "[": "]", "{": "}"}
32: _CLOSE = {v: k for k, v in _OPEN.items()}

35: def unbalanced(text: str) -> Optional[str]:
36:     """Why ``text`` has unbalanced brackets, or None when it is balanced.
37: 
38:     Mathematica strings ("...") and comments ((* ... *), nested) are skipped. An
39:     unbalanced verbatim string renders into a .fr that FeynRules stops reading
40:     with "Unexpected end of file" or "Invalid syntax", long after the schema
41:     said OK.
42:     """
43:     stack: List[Tuple[str, int]] = []
44:     i, n, depth = 0, len(text), 0
45:     while i < n:
46:         c = text[i]
47:         if depth:                                  # inside a comment
48:             if text.startswith("(*", i):
49:                 depth, i = depth + 1, i + 2
50:             elif text.startswith("*)", i):
51:                 depth, i = depth - 1, i + 2
52:             else:
53:                 i += 1
54:             continue
55:         if text.startswith("(*", i):
56:             depth, i = 1, i + 2
57:             continue
58:         if c == '"':                               # string literal
59:             i += 1
60:             while i < n and text[i] != '"':
61:                 i += 2 if text[i] == "\\" else 1
62:             if i >= n:
63:                 return "unterminated string literal"
64:             i += 1
65:             continue
66:         if c in _OPEN:
67:             stack.append((c, i))
68:         elif c in _CLOSE:
69:             if not stack or stack[-1][0] != _CLOSE[c]:
70:                 ctx = text[max(0, i - 30):i + 1]
71:                 return f"unexpected '{c}' at character {i} (...{ctx})"
72:             stack.pop()
73:         i += 1
74:     if depth:
75:         return "unterminated comment"
76:     if stack:
77:         c, j = stack[-1]
78:         ctx = text[j:j + 30]
79:         return f"'{c}' at character {j} is never closed ({ctx}...)"
80:     return None
81:

83: def _require_balanced(text: Optional[str], where: str) -> None:

85:         why = unbalanced(text)
86:         if why:

108:             "product with a symbol; write it as \"1.*^12\""

110:     if names or not re.search(r"[0-9]", s) or unbalanced(s):
111:         raise ValueError(
112:             f"{where}: value {s!r} is not a number, \"Internal\" or \"Automatic\" "
113:             "(FeynRules rejects anything else, e.g. \"Auto\" or \"External\"); "
114:             "use a numeric string such as \"1500.\" or \"2.5*^-3\""

384: def _references(text: str, name: str) -> bool:
385:     """True if ``name`` appears in ``text`` as a whole Mathematica token."""
386:     if not text:
387:         return False

391: def _param_refs(p: Parameter, names: set) -> set:
392:     """Names of other parameters referenced by ``p``'s value/rules/definitions."""
393:     texts: List[str] = []
394:     if p.value:
395:         texts.append(p.value)
396:     for r in p.value_rules:
397:         texts.append(r.rhs)
398:     for r in p.definitions:
399:         texts.append(r.rhs)
400:     blob = " ".join(texts)
401:     return {n for n in names if n != p.name and _references(blob, n)}

404: def topo_sort_parameters(params: List[Parameter]) -> List[Parameter]:
405:     """Order parameters so each is defined before others that reference it.
406: 
407:     Stable (preserves input order among independent params). Raises on a
408:     dependency cycle.
409:     """
410:     names = {p.name for p in params}
411:     deps = {p.name: _param_refs(p, names) for p in params}
412:     by_name = {p.name: p for p in params}
413: 
414:     ordered: List[Parameter] = []
415:     emitted: set = set()
416:     remaining = [p.name for p in params]  # preserve input order
417: 
418:     while remaining:
419:         progressed = False
420:         still: List[str] = []
421:         for n in remaining:
422:             if deps[n] <= emitted:
423:                 ordered.append(by_name[n])
424:                 emitted.add(n)
425:                 progressed = True
426:             else:
427:                 still.append(n)
428:         remaining = still
429:         if not progressed:
430:             raise ValueError(
431:                 f"cyclic parameter dependency among: {sorted(remaining)}"
432:             )
433:     return ordered

439: def _block_entries(p: Parameter, sizes: Dict[str, int]) -> set:
440:     """The LHA entries (index tuples) an External parameter occupies in its block."""
441:     if not p.is_tensor:
442:         return {(p.order_block,)} if p.order_block is not None else set()
443:     entries = set()
444:     for r in p.value_rules:
445:         m = re.fullmatch(rf"\s*{re.escape(p.name)}\s*\[([0-9,\s]+)\]\s*", r.lhs)
446:         if m:
447:             entries.add(tuple(int(x) for x in m.group(1).split(",")))
448:     if entries:
449:         return entries
450:     ranges = [range(1, sizes.get(i, 3) + 1) for i in p.indices]
451:     out = {()}
452:     for rg in ranges:
453:         out = {e + (k,) for e in out for k in rg}
454:     return out

457: def _check_block_collisions(params: List[Parameter], sizes: Dict[str, int]) -> None:
458:     """External parameters that share an LHA block must not share an entry.
459: 
460:     FeynRules files an External tensor's entries under (block, i, j) and a
461:     scalar under (block, OrderBlock). Two parameters on one entry leave the UFO
462:     with one name defined twice, and MadGraph rejects the model ("name VLq1x1
463:     define multiple time"). Tensors of different rank in one block do not
464:     collide: GeneralU1's yN[i] and ynu[i,j] share a block and import cleanly.
465:     """
466:     by_block: Dict[str, List[Parameter]] = {}
467:     for p in params:
468:         if p.parameter_type == ParamType.External and p.block_name:
469:             by_block.setdefault(p.block_name, []).append(p)
470:     for block, ps in by_block.items():
471:         owner: Dict[tuple, str] = {}
472:         for p in ps:
473:             for e in sorted(_block_entries(p, sizes)):
474:                 if e in owner and owner[e] != p.name:
475:                     raise ValueError(
476:                         f"External parameters {owner[e]} and {p.name} both occupy "
477:                         f"block {block!r} entry {list(e)}: the UFO would define one "
478:                         "name twice. Give one of them its own block_name (or, for "
479:                         "scalars, its own order_block)"
480:                     )
481:                 owner[e] = p.name

197: \section{Heavy Neutrino Model}\label{sec:Theory}
198: 
199: For  
200: $i~(m) =1,\dots,3$, LH (light) states and 
201: $j~(m')=1,\dots,n$, right-handed (heavy) states,
202: chiral neutrinos can be expanded into mass eigenstates by the rotation
203: \begin{eqnarray}
204: \begin{pmatrix} \nu_{Li} \\  N_{Rj}^c \end{pmatrix}
205: =
206: \begin{pmatrix} 
207: U_{3\times3} && V_{3\times n} \\
208: X_{n\times3} && Y_{n\times n}
209: \end{pmatrix}
210: \begin{pmatrix} \nu_{m} \\ N_{m'}^c \end{pmatrix}.
211: \end{eqnarray}
212: After rotating the charged leptons into the mass basis, 
213: which we take to be the identity matrix for simplicity,
214: $U_{3 \times3}$ is the observed light neutrino mixing matrix and
215: $V_{3 \times n}$ parameterizes active-heavy mixing. 
216: In the notation of~\cite{Atre:2009rg}, the flavor state $\nu_{\ell}$ in the mass basis is
217: \begin{equation}
218:  \nu_{\ell} = \sum_{m=1}^{3} U_{\ell m}\nu_{m} + \sum_{m'=1}^{n}V_{\ell m'} N^{c}_{m'}.
219: \end{equation}
220: For simplicity, we consider only one heavy mass eigenstate, labeled by $N$. This does not affect our conclusions.
221: The interaction Lagrangian with EW bosons is then
222: \begin{eqnarray}
223:   \mathcal{L}_{\rm Int.} = 
224:   &-& \frac{g}{\sqrt{2}}W^+_\mu		\sum_{\ell=e}^\tau \sum_{m=1}^3 ~\overline{\nu_m} ~U_{\ell m}^*	~\gamma^\mu P_L\ell^-\nonumber\\
225:   &-& \frac{g}{\sqrt{2}}W^+_\mu		\sum_{\ell=e}^\tau 		~\overline{N^c} ~V_{\ell N}^* 	~\gamma^\mu P_L\ell^-\nonumber\\
226:   &-& \frac{g}{2\cos\theta_W}Z_\mu	\sum_{\ell=e}^\tau \sum_{m=1}^3	~\overline{\nu_m} ~U_{\ell m}^*	~\gamma^\mu P_L\nu_\ell\nonumber\\
227:   &-& \frac{g}{2\cos\theta_W}Z_\mu	\sum_{\ell=e}^\tau 		~\overline{N^c} ~V_{\ell N}^*	~\gamma^\mu P_L\nu_\ell\nonumber\\
228:   &-& \frac{g m_N}{2M_W} h	\sum_{\ell=e}^\tau 		~\overline{N^c} ~V_{\ell N}^*	 P_L\nu_\ell + \text{H.c.}
229:   \label{eq:Lagrangian}
230: \end{eqnarray}
231: 
232: 
233: Precise values of $V_{\ell N}$ are model-dependent and are constrained by oscillation and collider experiments, 
234: tests of lepton universality, and $0\nu\beta\beta$-decay~\cite{Atre:2009rg,Antusch:2014woa,deGouvea:2015euy}.
235: However, $V_{\ell N}$ factorize in $N$ production cross sections such that
236: \begin{equation}

238: \end{equation}

321: \begin{equation}
322:  0.5  \leq \mu/ \mu_0 \leq2.
323: \end{equation}
324: 
325: 
326: In our framework, the CC DY rate at NLO can be calculated via the \mgamc~commands:
327: \begin{verbatim}
328: > import model HeavyN_NLO
329: > define p  = u c d s b u~ c~ d~ s~ b~ g
330: > define j  = p
331: > define mu = mu+ mu-
332: > generate p p > n2 mu [QCD]
333: > output PP_Nl_NLO; launch;
334: \end{verbatim}
335: Similarly, the inclusive NC DY at NLO is calculated by
336: \begin{verbatim}
337: > define vv = vm vm~
338: > generate p p > n2 vv [QCD]
339: > output PP_Nv_NLO; launch;
340: \end{verbatim}
341: and the inclusive CC $\DYj$ NLO rate by
342: \begin{verbatim}
343: > generate p p > n2 mu j QED=2 QCD=1 [QCD]
344: > output PP_Nl1j_NLO; launch;
345: \end{verbatim}
346: 
347: 
348: GF is a loop-induced process, which are only recently~\cite{Hirschi:2015iia} supported by \mgamc.
349: Such fully automated computations at NLO are unavailable since the two-loop technology does not currently exist.
350: We therefore perform the LO calculation matched and merged with up to one additional jet via the MLM scheme \cite{Mangano:2006rw}.
351: We discard loops that are actually virtual corrections to the DY process
352: and keep only diagrams where gluons do not appears in the loop.
353: The inclusive, unmatched LO GF rate can be calculated with
354:  \begin{verbatim}
355: > generate g g > n2 vv [QCD]
356: > output GGF_Nv_LO; launch;
357: \end{verbatim}
358: {Note that the $h^*/Z^*$ interference vanishes due to $C$-invariance/Fury's theorem
359: and the (anti-) symmetric nature of the residual $h~(Z)$ coupling~\cite{Willenbrock:1985tj,Hessler:2014ssa}.}
360: 
361: 
362:

365:   \subfigure[]{	\includegraphics[width=0.47\textwidth]{heavyN_xsec_vs_mN_100TeV.eps}	\label{fig:xsec100TeV_mN}	}
366: \caption{
367: Heavy $N$ NLO production rate in (a) 14 and (b) 100 TeV $pp$ collisions as a function of $m_N$, 
368: divided by active-heavy mixing $\vert V_{\ell N}\vert^2$,
369: for the inclusive CC (circle) and NC (triangle) DY, $N\ell^\pm+1j$ (diamond), and VBF (upside-down triangle) processes, 
370: as well as the LO GF process matched up to $1j$ (star). Lower: Ratio of NLO and LO rates.}
371: \label{fig:xSec}
372: \end{figure*}

378: d\sigma(q_{1}q_{2}\rightarrow N \ell^\pm q_{1}' q_{2}') \sim 
379: \log\left(\cfrac{m_N^2}{M_W^2}\right)\log\left(\cfrac{m_N^2}{p_T^{j_\gamma 2}}\right).

1: #!/usr/bin/env python3
2: """Deterministic lints for an agent-written FeynRules add-on (.fr) file.
3: 
4: Every rule encodes one construct that broke a compile, a FeynRules check or a
5: MadGraph import in the benchmark (prompt_addendum_v3.txt rules 9-15 and the
6: repair-loop taxonomy). A lint runs in milliseconds on the text; the compile it
7: predicts takes up to 900 s.
8: 
9: Each finding carries the STAGE it predicts:
10:   compile  - FeynRules will not load or will not finish the model
11:   checks   - the model loads but a consistency check fails
12:   mg5      - the UFO is written but MadGraph rejects it
13:   harness  - the validation harness cannot pick the total Lagrangian
14:   warn     - FeynRules warns; the run may still pass
15: 
16: Library: ``lint_text(text) -> list[Finding]``. CLI: ``fr_lint.py file.fr``.
17: """
18: 
19: from __future__ import annotations
20: 
21: import json
22: import re
23: import sys
24: from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
25: from pathlib import Path
26: from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Set
27: 
28: HEPTAPOD = Path.home() / "Documents/Github/heptapod"
29: SM_FR = HEPTAPOD / "tools/feynrules/test_files/models/SM.fr"
30: 
31: # Mathematica built-ins and FeynRules symbols a class, parameter or index must
32: # not be named after (rule 10).
33: FR_SYMBOLS = {"HC", "CC", "FS", "DC", "del", "Eps", "Ga", "ProjP", "ProjM", "T",
34:               "Sig", "PauliSigma", "IndexDelta", "ME", "Index", "Indices", "Mass",
35:               "Width", "Value", "Unphysical", "Abelian"}
36: PROTECTED = {"N", "C", "D", "E", "I", "K", "O", "Pi", "Gamma", "Beta", "Zeta",
37:              "Sqrt", "Exp", "Log", "Sin", "Cos", "Tan", "Re", "Im", "Conjugate",
38:              "Sum", "Block", "Module", "Table", "If", "Which"}
39: 
40: # Names SM.fr declares: classes, class members, parameters, gauge groups, indices.
41: _SM_TEXT = SM_FR.read_text() if SM_FR.is_file() else ""
42: SM_CLASSES: Set[str] = set(re.findall(r"ClassName\s*->\s*(\w+)", _SM_TEXT))
43: SM_MEMBERS: Set[str] = set()
44: for _m in re.findall(r"ClassMembers\s*->\s*\{([^}]*)\}", _SM_TEXT):
45:     SM_MEMBERS |= {x.strip() for x in _m.split(",") if x.strip()}
46: _i = _SM_TEXT.find("M$Parameters")
47: SM_PARAMS: Set[str] = set(re.findall(r"^\s*(\w+)\s*==\s*\{", _SM_TEXT[_i:], re.M)) if _i >= 0 else set()
48: SM_GAUGE = {"U1Y", "SU2L", "SU3C"}
49: SM_INDICES = {"Generation", "Colour", "Gluon", "SU2D", "SU2W", "Lorentz", "Spin",
50:               "Spin1", "Spin2", "Sextet"}
51: SM_FIELDS_ALL = SM_CLASSES | SM_MEMBERS | {c + "bar" for c in SM_CLASSES | SM_MEMBERS}
52: SM_MASSES = {"MZ", "MW", "MH", "Me", "MMU", "MTA", "MU", "MC", "MT", "MD", "MS", "MB",
53:              "WZ", "WW", "WH", "WT"}
54: 
55: FR_BUILTINS = {"HC", "CC", "FS", "DC", "del", "Eps", "Ga", "ProjP", "ProjM", "T",
56:                "PauliSigma", "IndexDelta", "ME", "Sqrt", "Exp", "Log", "Sin", "Cos",
57:                "Tan", "I", "Pi", "Sum", "Block", "Module", "ExpandIndices",
58:                "FlavorExpand", "True", "False", "bar", "anti", "left", "right",
59:                "Conjugate", "Re", "Im", "Abs", "Sig", "Ta", "T6", "K6", "K6bar",
60:                "K3", "K3bar", "f", "dSUN", "Dot", "Times", "Plus", "Power",
61:                "Automatic", "Internal", "External", "Unfold", "NoUnfold", "Range",
62:                "Index", "Lorentz", "Spin", "Colour", "Gluon", "Generation",
63:                "SU2D", "SU2W", "Sextet", "IndexStyle", "MakeIdenticalFermions",
64:                "Expand", "Simplify", "ProjPlus", "ProjMinus", "FR$", "vev"}

66: 
67: @dataclass
68: class Finding:
69:     rule: str
70:     stage: str  # compile | checks | mg5 | harness | warn
71:     message: str
72:     line: Optional[int] = None
73: 
74: 
75: # ------------------------------------------------------------------ parsing
76: 
77: def strip_comments(text: str) -> str:
78:     out, depth, i = [], 0, 0
79:     while i < len(text):
80:         if text.startswith("(*", i):
81:             depth += 1
82:             i += 2
83:             continue
84:         if text.startswith("*)", i) and depth:
85:             depth -= 1
86:             i += 2
87:             continue
88:         if depth == 0:
89:             out.append(text[i])
90:         elif text[i] == "\n":
91:             out.append("\n")
92:         i += 1
93:     return "".join(out)
94: 
95: 
96: def _matching(text: str, open_idx: int) -> int:
97:     depth = 0
98:     pairs = {"{": "}", "[": "]", "(": ")"}
99:     closes = set(pairs.values())
100:     for j in range(open_idx, len(text)):
101:         ch = text[j]
102:         if ch in pairs:
103:             depth += 1
104:         elif ch in closes:
105:             depth -= 1
106:             if depth == 0:
107:                 return j
108:     return len(text) - 1
109: 
110: 
111: def _block(text: str, name: str) -> str:
112:     m = re.search(rf"M\${name}\s*=\s*\{{", text)
113:     if not m:
114:         return ""
115:     end = _matching(text, m.end() - 1)
116:     return text[m.end():end]
117: 
118: 
119: def _entries(block: str) -> List[Dict]:
120:     """Top-level `Head == { ... }` entries of a M$ block."""
121:     out = []
122:     for m in re.finditer(r"(\w+(?:\[\s*\d+\s*\])?)\s*==\s*\{", block):
123:         end = _matching(block, m.end() - 1)
124:         body = block[m.end():end]
125:         out.append({"head": m.group(1), "body": body, "pos": m.start()})
126:     return out
127: 
128: 
129: def _prop(body: str, key: str) -> Optional[str]:
130:     m = re.search(rf"\b{key}\s*->\s*", body)
131:     if not m:
132:         return None
133:     rest = body[m.end():]
134:     if rest.startswith("{"):
135:         return rest[: _matching(rest, 0) + 1]
136:     mm = re.match(r"[^,}\n]+", rest)
137:     return mm.group(0).strip() if mm else None
138: 
139: 
140: def _is_kin_name(name: str) -> bool:
141:     return bool(re.search(r"kin|Kin|KIN|free|Free|Gauge|gauge", name))
142: 
143: 
144: def term_defs(text: str) -> List[Dict]:
145:     starts = [(m.group(1), m.start()) for m in re.finditer(r"^(L\w+)\s*:?=", text, re.M)]
146:     stops = [m.start() for m in re.finditer(r"^(?:M\$\w+\s*=|L\w+\s*:?=|\w+\s*=\s*\{)", text, re.M)]
147:     out = []
148:     for name, s in starts:
149:         e = min([x for x in stops if x > s] + [len(text)])
150:         out.append({"name": name, "body": text[s:e], "line": text[:s].count("\n") + 1})
151:     return out
152: 
153: 
154: def _line_of(text: str, needle: str) -> Optional[int]:
155:     i = text.find(needle)
156:     return text[:i].count("\n") + 1 if i >= 0 else None
157: 
158: 
159: # -------------------------------------------------------------------- lints
160: 
161: def lint_text(raw: str) -> List[Finding]:
162:     text = strip_comments(raw)
163:     F: List[Finding] = []
164:     classes = _entries(_block(text, "ClassesDescription"))
165:     params = _entries(_block(text, "Parameters"))
166:     terms = term_defs(text)
167:     term_names = {t["name"] for t in terms}
168:     term_bodies = "\n".join(t["body"] for t in terms)
169: 
170:     class_names, class_idx = {}, {}
171:     for c in classes:
172:         cn = _prop(c["body"], "ClassName")
173:         if cn:
174:             class_names[cn] = c
175:             mi = re.match(r"(\w+)\[\s*(\d+)\s*\]", c["head"])
176:             if mi:
177:                 class_idx[cn] = (mi.group(1), int(mi.group(2)))
178:     param_names = {p["head"]: p for p in params}
179:     index_decls = dict(re.findall(r"IndexRange\[\s*Index\[(\w+)\]\s*\]\s*=\s*([^;\n]+)", text))
180: 
181:     # --- rule 10: names -------------------------------------------------
182:     for name in list(class_names) + list(param_names) + list(index_decls):
183:         if name in FR_SYMBOLS:
184:             F.append(Finding("feynrules_symbol_name", "compile",
185:                              f"`{name}` is a FeynRules symbol", _line_of(text, name)))
186:         elif name in PROTECTED:
187:             F.append(Finding("protected_name", "warn",
188:                              f"`{name}` is a Mathematica built-in (loads with a warning; renaming is safer)",
189:                              _line_of(text, name)))
190:     for name in class_names:
191:         if name in SM_CLASSES or name in SM_MEMBERS:
192:             F.append(Finding("sm_class_redeclared", "warn",
193:                              f"class `{name}` is already declared by SM.fr (doubly-defined class)",
194:                              _line_of(text, f"ClassName -> {name}")))
195:     for name in param_names:
196:         if name in SM_PARAMS or name in SM_MASSES:
197:             F.append(Finding("sm_parameter_redeclared", "warn",
198:                              f"parameter `{name}` is already declared by SM.fr", _line_of(text, name)))
199:     for cn, c in class_names.items():
200:         for key in ("ParticleName", "AntiParticleName"):
201:             v = _prop(c["body"], key)
202:             names = re.findall(r'"([^"]*)"', v) if v else []
203:             if v and any(re.search(r"[\'`\s!@#%^&*()=\[\]{}|\\;:<>?/,]", nm) for nm in names):

205:                                  f"class `{cn}`: {key} {v} is not a valid UFO identifier", _line_of(text, v)))
206:         if cn in class_idx and class_idx[cn][1] < 100:

209:                              _line_of(text, c["head"])))
210:         for m in re.finditer(r"ClassMembers\s*->\s*\{([^}]*)\}", c["body"]):
211:             for mem in [x.strip() for x in m.group(1).split(",") if x.strip()]:
212:                 if mem in SM_MEMBERS or mem in SM_CLASSES:
213:                     F.append(Finding("sm_member_redeclared", "compile",
214:                                      f"class member `{mem}` of `{cn}` collides with an SM.fr name",
215:                                      _line_of(text, mem)))
216:     if "$" in re.sub(r"M\$\w+", "", text):
217:         for m in re.finditer(r"\b\w*\$\w*", text):
218:             if not re.match(r"^(M|MR|FR)\$", m.group(0)):

"""Deterministic lints for an agent-written FeynRules add-on (.fr) file.

Every rule encodes one construct that broke a compile, a FeynRules check or a
MadGraph import in the benchmark (prompt_addendum_v3.txt rules 9-15 and the
repair-loop taxonomy). A lint runs in milliseconds on the text; the compile it
predicts takes up to 900 s.

Each finding carries the STAGE it predicts:
  compile  - FeynRules will not load or will not finish the model
  checks   - the model loads but a consistency check fails
  mg5      - the UFO is written but MadGraph rejects it
  harness  - the validation harness cannot pick the total Lagrangian
  warn     - FeynRules warns; the run may still pass

Library: ``lint_text(text) -> list[Finding]``. CLI: ``fr_lint.py file.fr``.
"""
